📚 本期文献进展 / Literature Brief

  • 本期SARS-CoV-2研究集中呈现以下进展。
  • 在 Omicron 期间,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染率从 3% 增加到 24%,然后下降到零,最后上升到 10%。中和抗体总体从 18% 增加到 86%,几何平均值从 0.42 U/mL 增加到 9.4 U/mL。女性的 Nab 含量高于男性,并且 Nab 的数量随着年龄的增长而增加。
  • 共有 1471 名参与者参与其中。在队列研究 1中,与一剂BNT162b2相比,一剂或两剂BNT162b2-BA.1后的GMR分别为2.87和2.64。一剂和两剂 BNT162b2-BA.1 的血清反应差异分别为 29.0% 和 21.0%。
  • 在小鼠中,鼻内 AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N 引发了有效且持久的粘膜和全身免疫,包括血清/唾液 IgA 和持续长达 40 周的广泛中和抗体,以及组织局部的 B 和 T 细胞。
  • 奇异最小二乘估计在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 症状表现与所有选定的经济反应之间建立了正向且具有统计显着性的关系,递归二元概率证实了这些结果,但主动职业流动性除外,当考虑到未观察到的干扰的非线性和相关性时,主动职业流动性失去了统计显着性。
  • This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
  • SARS-CoV-2 infection rates increased from 3% to 24% then decreased to zero before rising to 10% during Omicron.
  • A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1, GMRs after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses were 2.87 and 2.64, respectively, compared with one BNT162b2 dose.
  • In mice, intranasal AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N elicited potent and durable mucosal and systemic immunity, including serum/saliva IgA and broad neutralizing antibodies persisting up to 40 weeks, alongside tissue-localized B and T cells.
  • Kinky least squares estimates establish a positive and statistically significant relationship between SARS-CoV-2 symptomatic manifestations and all selected economic responses, with the recursive bivariate probit confirming these results except for active occupational mobility, which loses statistical significance when accounting for non-linearity and correlation of unobserved disturbances.

Ensitrelvir for the Treatment of Hospitalized Adults With COVID-19: An International Phase 3 Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.

Ensitrelvir for the Treatment of Hospitalized Adults With COVID-19: An International Phase 3 Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.
作者： Jason V Baker, Lianne K Siegel, Marcelo H Losso, Shikha Vasudeva, Jacqueline A Nordwall, Katrina Harper, Birgit Grund, Joshua P Havens, Courtney V Fletcher, Roman Fishchuk
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
Antivirals remain an important treatment strategy for persons who experience severe and life-threatening COVID-19. Ensitrelvir is an oral 3CL protease inhibitor with potent antiviral activity.
设计与对象
We conducted an international randomized, placebo-controlled trial of ensitrelvir with standard of care (SOC) among adults hospitalized for COVID-19. Median age was 69 years, 49% were female, 68% were White, and SOC commonly included corticosteroids (61% and 54%) and remdesivir (62% and 60%) in ensitrelvir and placebo groups, respectively.
核心方法
主要结局是通过第 60 天的恢复天数 (DRS-60) 评估临床恢复情况,并使用 Van Elteren 测试进行分析。
主要结果
From 2023 to 2025, 589 participants received blinded study treatment (293 ensitrelvir and 296 placebo). Median DRS-60 category was 6 (IQR: 3-15) in the ensitrelvir and 5.5 (IQR: 3-12) in the placebo group (P = .19), and the OR was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.62-1.09) for a better DRS-60 category with ensitrelvir. Ensitrelvir participants had lower detectable viral antigen in plasma at Day 5 (13.4% vs 25.1%; P < .001).
解释与创新
Ensitrelvir treatment did not improve clinical recovery in addition to SOC for adults hospitalized for COVID-19. The lower illness severity in the Omicron era compared with earlier periods in the COVID-19 pandemic and high use of remdesivir and corticosteroids, may have contributed to the lack of clinical benefit.
科研与公卫意义
The findings suggest that ensitrelvir may reduce viral antigen levels in hospitalized COVID-19 patients but does not provide additional clinical benefit when combined with standard treatments. This information can inform future treatment strategies and research on antiviral therapies for COVID-19.
局限与证据强度
该研究是一项随机、安慰剂对照试验,样本量较大,但缺乏临床获益可能是由于 Omicron 时代疾病严重程度较低以及瑞德西韦和皮质类固醇的大量使用的影响。由于这些潜在的混杂因素,证据强度中等。

Ensitrelvir for the Treatment of Hospitalized Adults With COVID-19: An International Phase 3 Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.

Authors: Jason V Baker, Lianne K Siegel, Marcelo H Losso, Shikha Vasudeva, Jacqueline A Nordwall, Katrina Harper, Birgit Grund, Joshua P Havens, Courtney V Fletcher, Roman Fishchuk
Original abstract (English)
BACKGROUND: Antivirals remain an important treatment strategy for persons who experience severe and life-threatening COVID-19. Ensitrelvir is an oral 3CL protease inhibitor with potent antiviral activity. METHODS: We conducted an international randomized, placebo-controlled trial of ensitrelvir with standard of care (SOC) among adults hospitalized for COVID-19. The primary outcome was clinical recovery assessed by the days to recovery scale through day 60 (DRS-60), analyzed using a Van Elteren test. RESULTS: From 2023 to 2025, 589 participants received blinded study treatment (293 ensitrelvir and 296 placebo). Median age was 69 years, 49% were female, 68% were White, and SOC commonly included corticosteroids (61% and 54%) and remdesivir (62% and 60%) in ensitrelvir and placebo groups, respectively. Median DRS-60 category was 6 (IQR: 3-15) in the ensitrelvir and 5.5 (IQR: 3-12) in the placebo group (P = .19), and the OR was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.62-1.09) for a better DRS-60 category with ensitrelvir. Ensitrelvir participants had lower detectable viral antigen in plasma at Day 5 (13.4% vs 25.1%; P < .001). There was no difference in secondary clinical outcomes or prespecified safety outcomes, though the mortality rate was 6.1% vs 4.4% and the frequency of hemorrhagic events was 3.4% vs 0.3% among ensitrelvir and placebo groups, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Ensitrelvir treatment did not improve clinical recovery in addition to SOC for adults hospitalized for COVID-19. The lower illness severity in the Omicron era compared with earlier periods in the COVID-19 pandemic and high use of remdesivir and corticosteroids, may have contributed to the lack of clinical benefit.

Question and background
Antivirals remain an important treatment strategy for persons who experience severe and life-threatening COVID-19. Ensitrelvir is an oral 3CL protease inhibitor with potent antiviral activity.
Design and population
We conducted an international randomized, placebo-controlled trial of ensitrelvir with standard of care (SOC) among adults hospitalized for COVID-19. Median age was 69 years, 49% were female, 68% were White, and SOC commonly included corticosteroids (61% and 54%) and remdesivir (62% and 60%) in ensitrelvir and placebo groups, respectively.
Core methods
The primary outcome was clinical recovery assessed by the days to recovery scale through day 60 (DRS-60), analyzed using a Van Elteren test.
Main results
From 2023 to 2025, 589 participants received blinded study treatment (293 ensitrelvir and 296 placebo). Median DRS-60 category was 6 (IQR: 3-15) in the ensitrelvir and 5.5 (IQR: 3-12) in the placebo group (P = .19), and the OR was 0.82 (95% CI: 0.62-1.09) for a better DRS-60 category with ensitrelvir. Ensitrelvir participants had lower detectable viral antigen in plasma at Day 5 (13.4% vs 25.1%; P < .001).
Interpretation and novelty
Ensitrelvir treatment did not improve clinical recovery in addition to SOC for adults hospitalized for COVID-19. The lower illness severity in the Omicron era compared with earlier periods in the COVID-19 pandemic and high use of remdesivir and corticosteroids, may have contributed to the lack of clinical benefit.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings suggest that ensitrelvir may reduce viral antigen levels in hospitalized COVID-19 patients but does not provide additional clinical benefit when combined with standard treatments. This information can inform future treatment strategies and research on antiviral therapies for COVID-19.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study was a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with a large sample size, but the lack of clinical benefit may have been influenced by the lower illness severity in the Omicron era and high use of remdesivir and corticosteroids. The evidence strength is moderate due to these potential confounding factors.

Challenges and Opportunities for Signal Detection During Public Health Emergencies: An Historical Re-evaluation of the Disproportionality Analysis of the ADR Reporting of Anti-COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibodies in Vigibase.

Challenges and Opportunities for Signal Detection During Public Health Emergencies: An Historical Re-evaluation of the Disproportionality Analysis of the ADR Reporting of Anti-COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibodies in Vigibase.
作者： Nicoletta Luxi, Chiara Bellitto, Francesco Ciccimarra, Fabio Scapini, Elena Arzenton, Francesco Maccarrone, Ugo Moretti, Emanuel Raschi, Elisabetta Poluzzi, Daniele Focosi
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
该研究旨在通过使用 VigiBase 的不成比例性分析来识别抗 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 单克隆抗体的未探索的安全信号,因为新型病毒变体的不断出现需要快速的利益-风险评估。
设计与对象
2020 年 2 月至 2023 年 12 月对 VigiBase 进行了不成比例分析,重点关注特定抗 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 单克隆抗体的去重复个例安全报告。分析包括 bamlanivimab、bamlanivimab/etesevimab、casirivimab/imdevimab、regdanvimab、sotrovimab 和 tixagevimab/cilgavimab 的报告。
核心方法
该研究对个案安全性报告进行了描述性分析,并计算了 MedDRA 首选术语 (PT) 水平上 95% 置信区间 (CI) 的报告比值比 (ROR),使用整个数据库作为参考,同时排除 疫苗。
主要结果
在 15,250 份去重 ICSR 中,casirivimab/imdevimab 占报告的大部分(33.5%)。EMA 重要医疗事件 (IME) 列表中包含的具有统计学意义的药物不良反应对(未在产品特性摘要 (SmPC) 中描述)被确定为潜在的安全信号。
解释与创新
作者将这些发现解释为确定了某些抗 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 单克隆抗体的潜在心血管和神经安全信号,这些信号之前在 SmPC 中没有记录。
科研与公卫意义
研究结果强调了在公共卫生紧急情况下近实时多模式信号检测方法的重要性,特别是对于监测抗 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 单克隆抗体的安全性。
局限与证据强度
该研究的证据受到不成比例分析的回顾性和报告偏差的可能性的限制,由于依赖现有的药物警戒数据,因此具有中等的置信水平。

Challenges and Opportunities for Signal Detection During Public Health Emergencies: An Historical Re-evaluation of the Disproportionality Analysis of the ADR Reporting of Anti-COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibodies in Vigibase.

Authors: Nicoletta Luxi, Chiara Bellitto, Francesco Ciccimarra, Fabio Scapini, Elena Arzenton, Francesco Maccarrone, Ugo Moretti, Emanuel Raschi, Elisabetta Poluzzi, Daniele Focosi
Original abstract (English)
INTRODUCTION: Anti-spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for early treatment of COVID-19 represented a significant improvement in the pharmacological management of the SARS-COV-2 pandemic, especially in early phases, but the continuous emergence of novel virus variants of concern (VoC) required a rapid and continuous benefit-risk assessment. OBJECTIVE: To identify possible unexplored safety signals of anti-SARS-CoV-2 mAbs through disproportionality analysis using VigiBase, the World Health Organization (WHO) global pharmacovigilance database. METHODS: We conducted a disproportionality analysis of VigiBase (February 2020-December 2023). All de-duplicated individual case safety reports (ICSRs) for bamlanivimab, bamlanivimab/etesevimab, casirivimab/imdevimab, regdanvimab, sotrovimab, and tixagevimab/cilgavimab were retrieved. Descriptive analyses of ICSRs and distribution of suspected adverse drug reactions across VoC-defined periods (Alpha, Delta, Omicron) were performed. Disproportionality analysis was conducted and reported in accordance with the READUS-PV guideline. Reporting odds ratios (RORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated at the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) level, using the entire database as reference (excluding vaccines). Statistically significant drug-adverse reaction pairs included in the EMA Important Medical Event (IME) list and not described in the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) were identified as potential safety signals. RESULTS: Among 15,250 de-duplicated ICSRs, casirivimab/imdevimab accounted for the majority of reports (33.5%). Most cases involved female patients aged 45-64 years, predominantly reported from the Americas. Overall, 42,799 drug-adverse reaction pairs were identified, 33,948 (79.3%) of which were identified after filtering out, and 3047 (9.0%) were IMEs. Eighty-three unique drug-adverse reaction pairs had a statistically significant RORs, among which 56 (67.5%) were not listed in the SmPC. Bamlanivimab, as both monotherapy and in combination with etesevimab, showed increased reporting of several cardiac adverse events, including acute myocardial infarction (MI) and cardiac arrest. For tixagevimab/cilgavimab, disproportionality was found for acute MI (N = 6; ROR 12.7, 95% CI 5.7-28.4) and atrial fibrillation (N = 29; ROR 9.0, 95% CI 6.2-13.0). For regdanvimab, disproportionality emerged for hypokalemia (N = 13; ROR 5.8, 95% CI 3.4-10.1). For casirivimab/imdevimab, 5 out of 15 PTs were classified as adverse event of special interest: seizure-like phenomena (N = 8; ROR, 44.2; 95% CI 21.9-89.1), Guillain-Barré syndrome (N = 6; ROR 13.4, 95% CI 6.0-30.0), encephalopathy (N = 13; ROR 5.4, 95% CI 3.1-9.3), generalized tonic-clonic seizure (N = 9; ROR 5.0, 95% CI 2.6-9.7), and seizure (N = 57; ROR 3.1, 95% CI 2.4-4.0). CONCLUSION: This analysis identified potential cardiovascular and neurological safety signals, which will remain unexplored by longitudinal pharmacoepidemiologic studies due to the withdrawal of these agents from clinical use. Overall, this case study supported the full implementation of near real-time multimodal approaches to efficiently perform actionable signal management during public health emergencies.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study aimed to identify unexplored safety signals of anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies through disproportionality analysis using VigiBase, due to the continuous emergence of novel virus variants of concern requiring rapid benefit-risk assessment.
Design and population
A disproportionality analysis of VigiBase was conducted from February 2020 to December 2023, focusing on de-duplicated individual case safety reports for specific anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies. The analysis included reports for bamlanivimab, bamlanivimab/etesevimab, casirivimab/imdevimab, regdanvimab, sotrovimab, and tixagevimab/cilgavimab.
Core methods
The study performed descriptive analyses of individual case safety reports and calculated reporting odds ratios (RORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) at the MedDRA Preferred Term (PT) level, using the entire database as reference while excluding vaccines.
Main results
Among 15,250 de-duplicated ICSRs, casirivimab/imdevimab accounted for the majority of reports (33.5%). Statistically significant drug-adverse reaction pairs included in the EMA Important Medical Event (IME) list and not described in the Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) were identified as potential safety signals.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpreted the findings as identifying potential cardiovascular and neurological safety signals for certain anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies, which were not previously documented in the SmPC.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings highlight the importance of near real-time multimodal approaches for signal detection during public health emergencies, particularly for monitoring the safety of anti-SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study's evidence is limited by the retrospective nature of the disproportionality analysis and the potential for reporting biases, with a moderate confidence level due to the reliance on existing pharmacovigilance data.

编码 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 RBD 异二聚体的黑猩猩腺病毒载体 疫苗 的粘膜增强作用为小鼠提供了强大的保护

Mucosal boosting of chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored vaccine encoding SARS-CoV-2 RBD-heterodimer provides robust protection in mice
作者： Xueyuan Liu, Yaling An, Huixin Duan, Fei Shao, Kun Xu, Chenxi Yang, Senyu Xu, Xuemei Zhou, Minrun Duan, Tianyi Zheng
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
The study was needed because current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines, while effective against severe disease, have limited ability to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission, particularly in the upper respiratory tract where the virus primarily replicates.
设计与对象
该研究比较了 免疫应答 和 AdC68-Delta-XBB 疫苗 在小鼠模型中通过肌内注射、鼻内给药或气雾吸入给药的保护功效,并在加强剂后约 6 个月评估了针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 XBB.1 攻击的长期保护作用。
核心方法
研究人员构建了表达 Delta-XBB 受体结合域二聚体的黑猩猩腺病毒载体 疫苗,并评估了 免疫应答 和不同免疫途径后对小鼠的保护作用,包括评估肺部记忆 T 细胞和鼻组织中的病毒复制。
主要结果
AdC68-Delta-XBB 疫苗 的气雾吸入诱导了强大的全身和粘膜 免疫应答 和免疫记忆,特别是长时间激活肺部的记忆 T 细胞,与肌内注射相比,对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 XBB.1 攻击提供了明显更好的保护,鼻组织中没有检测到复制病毒。
解释与创新
作者解释说,气雾吸入 疫苗接种 对于强烈刺激全身和粘膜 免疫应答 特别有利,这项研究表明,AdC68-Delta-XBB 疫苗 通过气雾吸入诱导强劲的粘膜 免疫应答,以防止粘膜中的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染。
科研与公卫意义
These findings will guide future clinical development of mucosal vaccines against COVID-19 and provide a basis for developing vaccines against other respiratory pathogens, potentially offering more effective protection against infection and transmission.
局限与证据强度
证据强度中等,因为该研究是在小鼠模型中进行的,这可能无法完全转化为人类 免疫应答 和保护;然而,免疫途径的综合比较以及免疫应答和长期保护的评估为结论提供了实质性支持。

Mucosal boosting of chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored vaccine encoding SARS-CoV-2 RBD-heterodimer provides robust protection in mice

Authors: Xueyuan Liu, Yaling An, Huixin Duan, Fei Shao, Kun Xu, Chenxi Yang, Senyu Xu, Xuemei Zhou, Minrun Duan, Tianyi Zheng
Original abstract (English)
ABSTRACT The major route of COVID-19 vaccination currently is via intramuscular injection. Data from clinical trials and real-world studies have demonstrated its effectiveness in preventing severe illness and death caused by SARS-CoV-2 infection. However, its protective efficacy against SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission in situ remains relatively low. Given that SARS-CoV-2, especially the Omicron variant and its sub-variants, primarily infects and replicates in the human upper respiratory tract, mucosal immune responses are crucial for preventing viral infection. Therefore, we constructed a chimpanzee adenovirus (AdC68)-vectored vaccine expressing the Delta-XBB receptor-binding domain (RBD)-dimer and comprehensively compared the immune responses induced by intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation. Our results revealed that aerosol inhalation of the recombinant AdC68 vaccine induced robust systemic and mucosal immune responses and immune memory, particularly activating memory T cells in the lungs with a long duration in the mouse model. Additionally, we assessed long-term protection against a SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge after ~6 months following a booster vaccination with AdC68-Delta-XBB via different immunization routes. We found that, compared with the intramuscular route, aerosol inhalation provided significantly better protection, without detectable replicating virus in the nasal tissue. This study demonstrates that the AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine induces robust mucosal immune responses via aerosol inhalation vaccination and prevents SARS-CoV-2 infection in mucosa. IMPORTANCE Immunity induced by first-generation COVID-19 vaccines administered by intramuscular injection is highly effective against severe disease and death but is limited in its ability to prevent viral infection and transmission. A more cost-effective and practical vaccine delivered by the respiratory route is needed to better understand mucosal immune responses and to assess protective efficacy. This study evaluated the immune responses and protective efficacy elicited by intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation of AdC68-Delta-XBB in a mouse model and demonstrated that the aerosol inhalation approach is particularly advantageous for robustly stimulating both systemic and mucosal immune responses. These findings will help guide future clinical development and provide a basis for developing vaccines against other respiratory pathogens.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study was needed because current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines, while effective against severe disease, have limited ability to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection and transmission, particularly in the upper respiratory tract where the virus primarily replicates.
Design and population
The study compared immune responses and protective efficacy of an AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine delivered via intramuscular injection, intranasal administration, or aerosol inhalation in a mouse model, with long-term protection assessed against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge approximately 6 months post-booster.
Core methods
Researchers constructed a chimpanzee adenovirus-vectored vaccine expressing the Delta-XBB receptor-binding domain dimer and evaluated immune responses and protection in mice after different immunization routes, including assessment of memory T cells in the lungs and viral replication in nasal tissue.
Main results
Aerosol inhalation of the AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine induced robust systemic and mucosal immune responses and immune memory, particularly activating memory T cells in the lungs with long duration, and provided significantly better protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1 challenge compared to intramuscular injection, with no detectable replicating virus in nasal tissue.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpreted that aerosol inhalation vaccination is particularly advantageous for robustly stimulating both systemic and mucosal immune responses, and this study demonstrates that the AdC68-Delta-XBB vaccine induces robust mucosal immune responses via aerosol inhalation to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection in mucosa.
Scientific and public-health significance
These findings will guide future clinical development of mucosal vaccines against COVID-19 and provide a basis for developing vaccines against other respiratory pathogens, potentially offering more effective protection against infection and transmission.
Limitations and evidence strength
The evidence strength is moderate as the study was conducted in a mouse model, which may not fully translate to human immune responses and protection; however, the comprehensive comparison of immunization routes and assessment of both immune responses and long-term protection provide substantial support for the conclusions.

Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.

Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
作者： Shuko Nojiri, Tetsuya Takahashi, Yupeng Wang, Narimasa Katsuta, Hiroyuki Daida, Yuji Nishizaki
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
Physiotherapists played central roles in high-risk 'red-zone' care during COVID-19 and reported substantial distress, yet mechanisms linking exposure to burnout remain unclear.
设计与对象
We conducted a secondary analysis of a nationwide, multicentre, web-based survey of Japanese physiotherapists engaged in COVID-19 care (March 2021).
核心方法
倦怠是使用日本 MBI-GS 案例算法定义的。使用偏差校正和加速 (BCa) 引导程序(5,000 个重新采样)的反事实中介分析来估计平均因果中介效应 (ACME)、平均直接效应 (ADE) 和风险差异量表的总效应。模型根据年龄、性别、执业年限和同居情况进行了调整。
主要结果
倦怠 患病率 为 19.4%。观察到较小的间接效应(ACME = 0.00932;95% CI 0.00188-0.0200),而直接效应和总效应不具有统计显着性。欣赏/尊重与间接效应的减弱相关(ACME = 0.00007),而支持对危重患者的两名治疗师护理加强报销则与更大的间接效应相关(ACME = 0.00637;95% CI 0.00122-0.0100)。
解释与创新
Among Japanese physiotherapists, the association between direct COVID-19 patient contact and burnout was consistent with an indirect pathway operating through a stress-related behavioural mediator. Recognition appeared to buffer this pathway, whereas reimbursement-linked resource strain appeared to amplify it.
科研与公卫意义
这些发现表明了未来干预的潜在相关组织目标,但考虑到横断面设计和中介分析所需的因果假设,应谨慎解释。
局限与证据强度
由于主要中介分析使用了二元中介和具有逻辑联系函数的二元结果,因此在本规范下无法对未测量的中介-结果混杂进行正式的基于 ρ 的敏感性分析。由于横截面设计和对因果假设的依赖,证据强度中等。

Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.

Authors: Shuko Nojiri, Tetsuya Takahashi, Yupeng Wang, Narimasa Katsuta, Hiroyuki Daida, Yuji Nishizaki
Original abstract (English)
Background: Physiotherapists played central roles in high-risk 'red-zone' care during COVID-19 and reported substantial distress, yet mechanisms linking exposure to burnout remain unclear. Objective: To examine whether the association between direct patient contact and burnout operates through a stress-related behavioural mediator (feeling like quitting/taking a break) and whether organisational resources moderate this pathway. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of a nationwide, multicentre, web-based survey of Japanese physiotherapists engaged in COVID-19 care (March 2021). Burnout was defined using the Japanese MBI-GS case algorithm. Counterfactual mediation analysis with bias-corrected and accelerated (BCa) bootstraps (5,000 resamples) was used to estimate the average causal mediation effect (ACME), average direct effect (ADE), and total effect on the risk-difference scale. Models were adjusted for age, sex, years in practice, and cohabitation. Results: Burnout prevalence was 19.4%. A small indirect effect was observed (ACME = 0.00932; 95% CI 0.00188-0.0200), whereas the direct and total effects were not statistically significant. Appreciation/respect was associated with attenuation of the indirect effect (ACME = 0.00007), whereas endorsement of enhanced reimbursement for two-therapist care of critically ill patients was associated with a larger indirect effect (ACME = 0.00637; 95% CI 0.00122-0.0100). Because the primary mediation analysis used a binary mediator and binary outcome with logistic link functions, a formal ρ-based sensitivity analysis for unmeasured mediator-outcome confounding was not available under this specification. Conclusions: Among Japanese physiotherapists, the association between direct COVID-19 patient contact and burnout was consistent with an indirect pathway operating through a stress-related behavioural mediator. Recognition appeared to buffer this pathway, whereas reimbursement-linked resource strain appeared to amplify it. These findings suggest potentially relevant organisational targets for future intervention, but should be interpreted cautiously given the cross-sectional design and the causal assumptions required for mediation analysis.

在折叠稳定性和活性 imposed by fitness constraints 条件下 进化 的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 主要蛋白酶

Evolution of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease under fitness constraints imposed by folding stability and activity
作者： David Ferreiro, Miguel Arenas
摘要中文翻译摘要 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 不断进化和多样化,导致免疫逃避变异体的出现,并强调需要针对保守病毒机制的补充 抗病毒药物 策略。在这种情况下,主要蛋白酶(Mpro)代表了一个潜在的治疗靶点,因为它在病毒复制中发挥着核心作用,并且与人类蛋白酶的相似性较低。然而,Mpro 变异对底物识别和潜在抗性的进化后果尚未得到充分探索。通过对多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体的分析,我们表明,尽管病毒不断多样化,但自 2022 年 Omicron 相关 P132H 谱系出现以来,Mpro 进化 仍然受到显着限制,活性位点和二聚化界面区域的氨基酸替换有限。在最流行的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中,Mpro 的整体底物识别在很大程度上得以保留,尽管特定的变体-底物对在每个残基相互作用和氢键模式中表现出一些异质性。整体动力学揭示了某些 Mpro 变体中保守的大规模运动以及次级运动中适度的底物依赖性变化。总体而言,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 进化 受到结构和功能要求的强烈限制,支持该蛋白作为有效的 抗病毒药物 靶标的适用性。研究结果进一步表明,纳入病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有改善的长期稳健性的治疗策略。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
由于正在进行的 进化 和 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的多样化导致了免疫逃避变异,该研究解决了针对保守病毒机制的补充 抗病毒药物 策略的需求。它特别关注主要蛋白酶(Mpro)作为潜在的治疗靶点,因为它在病毒复制中发挥核心作用并且与人类蛋白酶的相似性较低。
设计与对象
该研究分析了多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变异,以研究 Mpro 变异对底物识别和潜在抗性的进化后果。
核心方法
通过对多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体的分析,该研究检查了活性位点和二聚化界面区域中的氨基酸取代,评估了底物识别,并评估了整体动力学,以了解某些 Mpro 变体中的大规模运动和次级运动。
主要结果
尽管病毒不断多样化,但自 2022 年 Omicron 相关 P132H 谱系出现以来,Mpro 进化 仍然受到显着限制,关键区域的氨基酸替换有限。尽管特定的变体-底物对在每个残基相互作用和氢键模式中表现出一些异质性,但 Mpro 的总体底物识别在最流行的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体中很大程度上保留了。
解释与创新
作者解释说,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 进化 受到结构和功能要求的强烈约束,支持其作为有效的 抗病毒药物 目标的适用性。新颖之处在于证明整合病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有改善的长期稳健性的治疗策略。
科研与公卫意义
研究结果支持 Mpro 作为有效 抗病毒药物 靶点的适用性,并表明纳入病毒进化动力学可能有助于设计具有更强长期稳健性的治疗策略,这对于应对不断变化的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异株至关重要。
局限与证据强度
该研究的证据强度很高,因为它直接分析了多个 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Mpro 变体,并提供了对其结构和功能限制的详细见解。然而,其局限性包括特定变体-底物对中每个残基相互作用和氢键模式可能存在一些异质性,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍性。

Evolution of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease under fitness constraints imposed by folding stability and activity

Authors: David Ferreiro, Miguel Arenas
Original abstract (English)
Abstract The severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) continues to evolve and diversify, leading to the emergence of immune-evasive variants and underscoring the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery. In this context, the main protease (Mpro) represents a potential therapeutic target because of its central role in viral replication and its low similarity to human proteases. However, the evolutionary consequences of Mpro variation on substrate recognition and potential resistance remain insufficiently explored. Through the analysis of multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants, we show that, despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions. Across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants, overall substrate recognition by Mpro was largely preserved, although specific variant-substrate pairs exhibited some heterogeneity in per-residue interactions and hydrogen-bond patterns. Ensemble dynamics revealed conserved large-scale motions alongside modest substrate-dependent shifts in secondary motions in certain Mpro variants. Overall, SARS-CoV-2 Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, supporting the suitability of this protein as an effective antiviral target. The findings further suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help inform the design of therapeutic strategies with improved long-term robustness.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study addresses the need for complementary antiviral strategies targeting conserved viral machinery due to the ongoing evolution and diversification of SARS-CoV-2, which has led to immune-evasive variants. It specifically focuses on the main protease (Mpro) as a potential therapeutic target due to its central role in viral replication and low similarity to human proteases.
Design and population
The study analyzed multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants to investigate the evolutionary consequences of Mpro variation on substrate recognition and potential resistance.
Core methods
Through the analysis of multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants, the study examined amino-acid substitutions in the active-site and dimerization-interface regions, assessed substrate recognition, and evaluated ensemble dynamics to understand large-scale motions and secondary motions in certain Mpro variants.
Main results
Despite ongoing viral diversification, Mpro evolution has remained remarkably constrained since the emergence of the Omicron-associated P132H lineage in 2022, with limited amino-acid substitutions in key regions. Overall substrate recognition by Mpro was largely preserved across the most prevalent SARS-CoV-2 variants, although specific variant-substrate pairs exhibited some heterogeneity in per-residue interactions and hydrogen-bond patterns.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpret that SARS-CoV-2 Mpro evolution is strongly constrained by structural and functional requirements, supporting its suitability as an effective antiviral target. The novelty lies in demonstrating that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help inform the design of therapeutic strategies with improved long-term robustness.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings support the suitability of Mpro as an effective antiviral target and suggest that incorporating viral evolutionary dynamics may help design therapeutic strategies with improved long-term robustness, which is crucial for combating evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study's evidence strength is high, as it directly analyzes multiple SARS-CoV-2 Mpro variants and provides detailed insights into their structural and functional constraints. However, the limitations include the potential for some heterogeneity in per-residue interactions and hydrogen-bond patterns in specific variant-substrate pairs, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

表达串联 RBD 和核衣壳的鼻内黑猩猩腺病毒 疫苗 对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 和 SARS-CoV 具有广泛而持久的保护作用

Broad and durable protection against SARS-CoV-2 and SARS-CoV by an intranasal chimpanzee adenovirus vaccine expressing tandem RBDs and nucleocapsid
作者： Yaping Liu, Runhong Zhou, Tian Zhao, Ruoke Wang, Kun Zhu, Junxian Hong, Ziqing Yang, Qianqian Yang, Yuqing Lei, Yang Bai
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
Current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines reduce severe disease but offer limited protection against infection, enabling viral persistence, immune escape, and transmission.
设计与对象
我们开发了基于鼻内稀有血清型黑猩猩腺病毒 68 (AdC68) 的 疫苗,表达来自 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、SARS-CoV 和 MERS-CoV 的异源串联受体结合域,与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳 (AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N) 融合,以增强 B 和 T 细胞反应。
核心方法
通过受体结合和多种构象敏感单克隆抗体的识别来确认抗原完整性。
主要结果
在小鼠中,鼻内 AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N 引发了有效且持久的粘膜和全身免疫,包括血清/唾液 IgA 和持续长达 40 周的广泛中和抗体,以及组织局部的 B 和 T 细胞。
解释与创新
来自长寿骨髓抗体分泌细胞的单克隆抗体表现出广泛的菌株特异性中和作用,为抗体反应的广度和寿命提供了机制上的见解。
科研与公卫意义
在叙利亚仓鼠中,鼻内免疫可防止 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 XBB.1.5 在鼻甲和肺部复制,并在 疫苗接种 后长达四个月内阻断 传播。
局限与证据强度
K18-hACE2 转基因小鼠证明了其对 SARS-CoV 攻击的强大保护作用,进一步证实了其广泛的功效。

Broad and durable protection against SARS-CoV-2 and SARS-CoV by an intranasal chimpanzee adenovirus vaccine expressing tandem RBDs and nucleocapsid

Authors: Yaping Liu, Runhong Zhou, Tian Zhao, Ruoke Wang, Kun Zhu, Junxian Hong, Ziqing Yang, Qianqian Yang, Yuqing Lei, Yang Bai
Original abstract (English)
Current intramuscular COVID-19 vaccines reduce severe disease but offer limited protection against infection, enabling viral persistence, immune escape, and transmission. We developed intranasal rare-serotype chimpanzee adenovirus 68 (AdC68)–based vaccines expressing heterologous tandem receptor-binding domains from SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, and MERS-CoV, fused to the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid (AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N) to enhance both B and T cell responses. Antigen integrity was confirmed by receptor binding and recognition by multiple conformation-sensitive monoclonal antibodies. In mice, intranasal AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N elicited potent and durable mucosal and systemic immunity, including serum/saliva IgA and broad neutralizing antibodies persisting up to 40 weeks, alongside tissue-localized B and T cells. Monoclonal antibodies from long-lived bone marrow antibody-secreting cells demonstrated broad and strain-specific neutralization, providing mechanistic insight into the breadth and longevity of the antibody response. In Syrian hamsters, intranasal immunization protected against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 replication in nasal turbinates and lungs and blocked transmission for up to four months post-vaccination. Robust protection against SARS-CoV challenge was demonstrated in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice, further confirming its broad efficacy. These findings support AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N as a promising mucosal vaccine candidate to prevent infection and transmission of pathogenic coronaviruses.

Core methods
Antigen integrity was confirmed by receptor binding and recognition by multiple conformation-sensitive monoclonal antibodies.
Main results
In mice, intranasal AdC68-4RBD(XBB.1.5)-N elicited potent and durable mucosal and systemic immunity, including serum/saliva IgA and broad neutralizing antibodies persisting up to 40 weeks, alongside tissue-localized B and T cells.
Interpretation and novelty
Monoclonal antibodies from long-lived bone marrow antibody-secreting cells demonstrated broad and strain-specific neutralization, providing mechanistic insight into the breadth and longevity of the antibody response.

Robust protection against SARS-CoV challenge was demonstrated in K18-hACE2 transgenic mice, further confirming its broad efficacy.

Real-world effectiveness and safety of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (BEEHIVE trial).

Real-world effectiveness and safety of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (BEEHIVE trial).
作者： Sarang K. Yoon, Andrew L. Phillips, S. Battan-Wraith, Matthew S Thiese, E. Rowley, G. L. Ellsworth, R. Fink, Danli Chen, Adam Yates, Feiyun Yan
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
Real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) and relative VE (rVE) data of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections inform policy recommendations and reinforce public confidence.
设计与对象
The single-site, pragmatic BEEHIVE clinical trial was conducted among participants aged ≥18 years from the Salt Lake City, Utah, area, who had previously received ≥2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, from November 17, 2023, through September 9, 2024.
核心方法
Randomized participants received a protein-based or mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in a double-blind manner, with an unblinded, nonrandomized comparator control group that did not receive a study vaccine. VE and rVE were estimated using a proportional-hazards model for symptomatic infections confirmed by weekly self-administered rapid antigen tests (RATs) over 24 weeks, adjusted for covariates.
主要结果
Randomized cohorts (N = 909; protein-based, n = 452; mRNA, n = 457) were largely well-balanced with some differences in baseline covariates versus the comparator group (n = 279), mostly age-related. The mITT population had 142 RAT-confirmed symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 cases with an adjusted VE of 43.6% (95% CI, 18.3-61.0); rVE (protein-based vs mRNA) was -26.7% (90% CI, -78.6% to 10.1%) and did not reach statistical significance.
解释与创新
This is one of the earliest real-world trials evaluating the VE of the 2023-2024 COVID-19 vaccines (XBB.1.5). These results suggest that both protein-based and mRNA vaccines are well-tolerated and significantly reduce the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections.
科研与公卫意义
The findings provide real-world evidence supporting the use of both protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines for reducing symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections, informing policy recommendations and public health strategies.
局限与证据强度
该研究是一项单中心试验,比较组不是随机的,这可能会引入偏差。由于务实的设计和组间存在一些基线差异,证据强度中等。

Real-world effectiveness and safety of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (BEEHIVE trial).

Authors: Sarang K. Yoon, Andrew L. Phillips, S. Battan-Wraith, Matthew S Thiese, E. Rowley, G. L. Ellsworth, R. Fink, Danli Chen, Adam Yates, Feiyun Yan
Original abstract (English)
BACKGROUND Real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) and relative VE (rVE) data of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections inform policy recommendations and reinforce public confidence. The study aim was to assess the safety and VE of the 2023-2024 protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines (XBB.1.5) in a real-world setting. METHODS The single-site, pragmatic BEEHIVE clinical trial was conducted among participants aged ≥18 years from the Salt Lake City, Utah, area, who had previously received ≥2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, from November 17, 2023, through September 9, 2024. Randomized participants received a protein-based or mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in a double-blind manner. An unblinded, nonrandomized comparator control group that did not receive a study vaccine was also enrolled. The primary aim measured VE between the randomized and comparator groups. The secondary aim was to measure rVE between the 2 vaccine platforms. In the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis, VE and rVE were estimated using a proportional-hazards model for symptomatic infections confirmed by weekly self-administered rapid antigen tests (RATs) over 24 weeks, adjusted for covariates. Reactogenicity and treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were recorded. RESULTS Randomized cohorts (N = 909; protein-based, n = 452; mRNA, n = 457) were largely well-balanced with some differences in baseline covariates versus the comparator group (n = 279), mostly age-related. The mITT population had 142 RAT-confirmed symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 cases with an adjusted VE of 43.6% (95% CI, 18.3-61.0); rVE (protein-based vs mRNA) was -26.7% (90% CI, -78.6% to 10.1%) and did not reach statistical significance. Safety and reactogenicity were comparable to previously reported findings, with no serious study vaccine-related TEAEs, myocarditis/pericarditis, hospitalization, or death. CONCLUSIONS This is one of the earliest real-world trials evaluating the VE of the 2023-2024 COVID-19 vaccines (XBB.1.5). These results suggest that both protein-based and mRNA vaccines are well-tolerated and significantly reduce the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections.

Question and background
Real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) and relative VE (rVE) data of protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections inform policy recommendations and reinforce public confidence.
Design and population
The single-site, pragmatic BEEHIVE clinical trial was conducted among participants aged ≥18 years from the Salt Lake City, Utah, area, who had previously received ≥2 mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, from November 17, 2023, through September 9, 2024.
Core methods
Randomized participants received a protein-based or mRNA COVID-19 vaccine in a double-blind manner, with an unblinded, nonrandomized comparator control group that did not receive a study vaccine. VE and rVE were estimated using a proportional-hazards model for symptomatic infections confirmed by weekly self-administered rapid antigen tests (RATs) over 24 weeks, adjusted for covariates.
Main results
Randomized cohorts (N = 909; protein-based, n = 452; mRNA, n = 457) were largely well-balanced with some differences in baseline covariates versus the comparator group (n = 279), mostly age-related. The mITT population had 142 RAT-confirmed symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 cases with an adjusted VE of 43.6% (95% CI, 18.3-61.0); rVE (protein-based vs mRNA) was -26.7% (90% CI, -78.6% to 10.1%) and did not reach statistical significance.
Interpretation and novelty
This is one of the earliest real-world trials evaluating the VE of the 2023-2024 COVID-19 vaccines (XBB.1.5). These results suggest that both protein-based and mRNA vaccines are well-tolerated and significantly reduce the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings provide real-world evidence supporting the use of both protein-based and mRNA COVID-19 vaccines for reducing symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections, informing policy recommendations and public health strategies.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study was a single-site trial with a comparator group that was not randomized, which may introduce bias. The evidence strength is moderate due to the pragmatic design and the presence of some baseline differences between groups.

部分封锁背景下严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的症状表现和家庭经济反应:基于喀麦隆家庭调查数据的分析

Symptomatic manifestations of SARS-CoV-2 and household economic responses in the context of partial lockdown: an analysis based on Cameroonian household survey data
作者： Gilchrist Bessoum Keedi, Benjamin Fomba Kamga
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
This article analyzes the economic responses of household heads confronted with SARS-CoV-2 symptoms during the partial lockdown period imposed in Cameroon in 2020, filling a gap in the literature on the economic effects of COVID-19 by isolating the specific effect of individual symptomatic shock from general health restrictions.
设计与对象
该研究基于喀麦隆的家庭调查数据,分析了五种经济反应:过度负债、积极的职业流动以及健康、教育和卫生保护支出的减少。
核心方法
为了解决内生性问题,采用了两种互补策略:扭结最小二乘法 (KLS) 和带有工具变量的递归二元概率,它们联合对二元 治疗 和结果进行建模,同时考虑其未观察到的误差项之间的相关性。
主要结果
奇异最小二乘估计在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 症状表现与所有选定的经济反应之间建立了正向且具有统计显着性的关系,递归二元概率证实了这些结果,但主动职业流动性除外,当考虑到未观察到的干扰的非线性和相关性时,主动职业流动性失去了统计显着性。
解释与创新
对平均 治疗 效应的分解表明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 症状表现使整个人口的卫生防护支出减少了 37.3%,受影响的户主减少了 38.1%,教育和医疗支出减少也观察到了类似的效果。
科研与公卫意义
这些调查结果支持免费分发卫生防护设备、补贴医疗咨询和社区药品库存、维持学校转移支付以及为暂时丧失工作能力的非正规工人提供零息紧急信贷额度。
局限与证据强度
证据强度适中,因为该研究通过补充统计方法解决了内生性问题,但承认只要健康覆盖体系仍然严重不发达,所提出的措施就仍然不够。

Symptomatic manifestations of SARS-CoV-2 and household economic responses in the context of partial lockdown: an analysis based on Cameroonian household survey data

Authors: Gilchrist Bessoum Keedi, Benjamin Fomba Kamga
Original abstract (English)
This article analyzes the economic responses of household heads confronted with SARS-CoV-2 symptoms during the partial lockdown period imposed in Cameroon in 2020. By isolating the specific effect of the individual symptomatic shock from that of general health restrictions, it fills a gap that the literature on the economic effects of COVID-19 has not yet directly addressed. The data come from a household survey conducted in Cameroon, and five economic responses are analyzed, namely over-indebtedness, active occupational mobility, and reductions in health, education, and sanitary protection expenditures. To address endogeneity, two complementary strategies are employed, namely the kinky least squares (KLS) method, which corrects endogeneity bias without resorting to an external instrument, and the recursive bivariate probit with instrumental variable, which jointly models binary treatment and outcome while accounting for the correlation between their unobserved error terms. Kinky least squares estimates establish a positive and statistically significant relationship between SARS-CoV-2 symptomatic manifestations and all of the selected economic responses. The recursive bivariate probit confirms these results, with the exception of active occupational mobility, whose coefficient remains positive but loses its statistical significance once non-linearity and the correlation of unobserved disturbances are fully accounted for. The decomposition of average treatment effects indicates that SARS-CoV-2 symptomatic manifestations increase the probability of reducing sanitary protection expenditures by 37.3% across the entire population (ATE) and by 38.1% among household heads who were actually affected (ATET). For education expenditures, these effects are 28.6% and 25.6%, respectively. For health expenditure reductions, these effects are 23.2% and 18.6%, respectively. These findings argue in favor of the free distribution of sanitary protection devices, the subsidization of medical consultations and community drug stockpiles, the maintenance of school transfer payments, and zero-interest emergency credit lines for informal workers experiencing temporary work incapacity. These measures will nonetheless remain insufficient as long as the health coverage system remains critically underdeveloped.

Question and background
This article analyzes the economic responses of household heads confronted with SARS-CoV-2 symptoms during the partial lockdown period imposed in Cameroon in 2020, filling a gap in the literature on the economic effects of COVID-19 by isolating the specific effect of individual symptomatic shock from general health restrictions.
Design and population
The study is based on household survey data from Cameroon, analyzing five economic responses: over-indebtedness, active occupational mobility, and reductions in health, education, and sanitary protection expenditures.
Core methods
To address endogeneity, two complementary strategies are employed: the kinky least squares (KLS) method and the recursive bivariate probit with instrumental variable, which jointly models binary treatment and outcome while accounting for the correlation between their unobserved error terms.
Main results
Kinky least squares estimates establish a positive and statistically significant relationship between SARS-CoV-2 symptomatic manifestations and all selected economic responses, with the recursive bivariate probit confirming these results except for active occupational mobility, which loses statistical significance when accounting for non-linearity and correlation of unobserved disturbances.
Interpretation and novelty
The decomposition of average treatment effects indicates that SARS-CoV-2 symptomatic manifestations increase the probability of reducing sanitary protection expenditures by 37.3% across the entire population and by 38.1% among affected household heads, with similar effects observed for education and health expenditure reductions.
Scientific and public-health significance
These findings argue in favor of the free distribution of sanitary protection devices, subsidization of medical consultations and community drug stockpiles, maintenance of school transfer payments, and zero-interest emergency credit lines for informal workers experiencing temporary work incapacity.
Limitations and evidence strength
The evidence strength is moderate, as the study addresses endogeneity through complementary statistical methods but acknowledges that the measures proposed will remain insufficient as long as the health coverage system remains critically underdeveloped.

Post COVID-19 condition diagnosis among older people: findings from Swedish national register data.

Post COVID-19 condition diagnosis among older people: findings from Swedish national register data.
作者： Zhongsong Zhang, Minh Tuan Hoang, Jonas W. Wastesson, Kristina Johnell
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
Post COVID-19 condition (PCC) denotes the persistence of symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection and poses a large disease burden worldwide.
设计与对象
这项全国性的登记研究采用横断面设计来探讨瑞典 65 岁以上老年人中临床诊断的 PCC 的流行病学特征。
核心方法
PCC 诊断 的 患病率 在医院和专科门诊护理环境中计算,并采用逻辑回归模型评估各种因素与 PCC 之间的关联,并构建基于极端梯度提升的预测模型。
主要结果
Of 236,943 older people diagnosed with COVID-19, 2.5% were diagnosed with PCC in hospital or specialized outpatient care; women had lower odds (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.82), and odds decreased with each additional year of age (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.98).
解释与创新
当仅限于医院和专门门诊护理时,瑞典老年人中 PCC 诊断 的 患病率 相对较低,基于登记的预测模型可能有助于识别 PCC 风险较高的老年人。
科研与公卫意义
研究结果可以为 PCC 风险较高的老年人,特别是那些合并症负担较高和药物使用较多的老年人提供有针对性的 监测 和早期干预策略。
局限与证据强度
由于依赖基于登记的数据,证据强度中等,这可能不足以代表未在医院或专门门诊护理中诊断的 PCC 病例。

Post COVID-19 condition diagnosis among older people: findings from Swedish national register data.

Authors: Zhongsong Zhang, Minh Tuan Hoang, Jonas W. Wastesson, Kristina Johnell
Original abstract (English)
INTRODUCTION: Post COVID-19 condition (PCC) denotes the persistence of symptoms following Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection. PCC poses a large disease burden worldwide. We aimed to explore the epidemiological characteristics of clinically diagnosed PCC among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden and to establish a machine learning tool to predict PCC risk. METHODS: This nationwide register-based study employed a cross-sectional design. Prevalence of PCC diagnosis recorded in hospital and specialized outpatient care settings among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden was calculated. Logistic regression models were employed to assess the associations between various factors and PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care. A prediction model based on extreme gradient boosting was constructed based on selected features. RESULTS: Of 236,943 older people aged ≥65 years who were diagnosed with COVID-19, 2.5% of them were diagnosed with PCC in hospital or specialized outpatient care. The odds of PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care in women were lower (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.82). The odds decreased for each additional year of age (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.98). Higher odds of PCC were found in people with higher Charlson Comorbidity Index and who used more types of medication. The odds of PCC were the lowest for infections during Omicron-predominant period (OR = 0.09, 95% CI: 0.08-0.10). The predicted PCC risk was generally higher among individuals aged 65-74 years with higher comorbidity burden, more types of medication use, and during early variant-dominant periods. CONCLUSION: In summary, the prevalence of PCC diagnosis among older people in Sweden was relatively low when restricted to hospital and specialized outpatient care. A higher burden of comorbidities and more types of medication use were associated with increased odds of PCC diagnosed in hospital and specialized outpatient care. Register-based predictive models may help identify older people at higher risk of PCC.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
Post COVID-19 condition (PCC) denotes the persistence of symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection and poses a large disease burden worldwide.
Design and population
This nationwide register-based study employed a cross-sectional design to explore the epidemiological characteristics of clinically diagnosed PCC among older people aged ≥65 years in Sweden.
Core methods
The prevalence of PCC diagnosis was calculated in hospital and specialized outpatient care settings, and logistic regression models were employed to assess associations between various factors and PCC, along with constructing a prediction model based on extreme gradient boosting.
Main results
Of 236,943 older people diagnosed with COVID-19, 2.5% were diagnosed with PCC in hospital or specialized outpatient care; women had lower odds (OR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.73-0.82), and odds decreased with each additional year of age (OR = 0.98, 95% CI: 0.98-0.98).
Interpretation and novelty
The prevalence of PCC diagnosis among older people in Sweden was relatively low when restricted to hospital and specialized outpatient care, and register-based predictive models may help identify older people at higher risk of PCC.
Scientific and public-health significance
Findings can inform targeted surveillance and early intervention strategies for older adults at higher risk of PCC, particularly those with higher comorbidity burden and more medication use.
Limitations and evidence strength
The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on register-based data, which may underrepresent PCC cases not diagnosed in hospital or specialized outpatient care.

严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳的深度突变扫描揭示了区域稳定性模式。

Deep mutational scanning of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid reveals regional stability patterns.
作者： Alasdair D Keith, Meredith M Keen, Filipp Frank, Eric A Ortlund
摘要中文翻译严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳蛋白 (NP) 内的点 突变 不仅有可能影响检测,还可能影响病毒生命周期,从而影响致病性。利用深度突变扫描 (DMS),我们确定所有可能点 突变 的 7876 个点 (98.9%) 对 NP 表面表达的影响作为稳定性的代理,我们将其称为基于表面表达的折叠适应度 (SEBFF)。我们发现 NP 对 SEBFF 变化的敏感性因区域而异,突变 对结构化 RNA 结合域 (RBD) 和二聚化域 (DD) 更有可能导致 SEBFF 减少。我们表明,连接区中的 R203K 突变 增加了 NP 的折叠适合度,这表明热稳定性可能是推动 α、γ 和 omicron 谱系中出现的 R203K/G204R 突变 组采用的因素之一。我们的 DMS 结果似乎与文献中可获得的 NP 变体的有限重组蛋白和生物物理数据一致。我们测试了三种计算方法,以确定是否有任何方法可以准确预测 DMS 数据;每个变体的预测很差,但每个位点的预测都很好,机器学习方法优于基于物理的策略,并且 ThermoMPNN-D 与 RBD 和 ProteinMPNN 与 DD 配合使用时表现最有效。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳蛋白 (NP) 内的点 突变 不仅有可能影响检测,还可能影响病毒生命周期,从而影响致病性。
设计与对象
利用深度突变扫描 (DMS),我们确定所有可能点 突变 的 7876 个点 (98.9%) 对 NP 表面表达的影响作为稳定性的代理,我们将其称为基于表面表达的折叠适应度 (SEBFF)。
核心方法
我们测试了三种计算方法,以确定是否有任何方法可以准确预测 DMS 数据;每个变体的预测很差,但每个位点的预测都很好,机器学习方法优于基于物理的策略,并且 ThermoMPNN-D 与 RBD 和 ProteinMPNN 与 DD 配合使用时表现最有效。
主要结果
我们发现 NP 对 SEBFF 变化的敏感性因区域而异,突变 对结构化 RNA 结合域 (RBD) 和二聚化域 (DD) 更有可能导致 SEBFF 减少。我们表明,连接区中的 R203K 突变 增加了 NP 的折叠适合度,这表明热稳定性可能是推动 α、γ 和 omicron 谱系中出现的 R203K/G204R 突变 组采用的因素之一。
解释与创新
我们的 DMS 结果似乎与文献中可获得的 NP 变体的有限重组蛋白和生物物理数据一致。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现提供了对 突变 在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 核衣壳蛋白中的功能影响的见解,这可能有助于 监测 策略和对病毒 进化 的理解。
局限与证据强度
该研究仅限于体外深度突变扫描和计算预测,没有在病毒复制系统中进行直接验证。由于突变覆盖全面,但缺乏体内证实,证据强度中等。

Deep mutational scanning of SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid reveals regional stability patterns.

Authors: Alasdair D Keith, Meredith M Keen, Filipp Frank, Eric A Ortlund
Original abstract (English)
Point mutations within the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (NP) have the potential to impact not only detection but the viral life cycle, and therefore pathogenicity. Leveraging deep mutational scanning (DMS) we determine the effect of 7876 (98.9%) of all possible point mutations on NP surface expression as a proxy for stability, which we term surface-expression-based folding fitness (SEBFF). We show NP susceptibility to SEBFF changes varies with region, with mutations to the structured RNA-binding domain (RBD) and dimerization domain (DD) being more likely to cause decreases in SEBFF. We show that the R203K mutation in the linker region increases the folding fitness of NP, suggesting thermostability may have been one factor driving the adoption of the R203K/G204R set of mutations arising in the alpha, gamma and omicron lineages. Our DMS results appear consistent with the limited recombinant protein and biophysical data for NP variants available from the literature. We tested three computational methods to determine whether any could accurately predict the DMS data; per-variant predictions were poor, but per-site predictions were good, with machine learning methods outperforming the physics-based strategy, and ThermoMPNN-D performing most effectively with the RBD and ProteinMPNN with the DD.

Question and background
Point mutations within the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein (NP) have the potential to impact not only detection but the viral life cycle, and therefore pathogenicity.
Design and population
Leveraging deep mutational scanning (DMS) we determine the effect of 7876 (98.9%) of all possible point mutations on NP surface expression as a proxy for stability, which we term surface-expression-based folding fitness (SEBFF).
Core methods
We tested three computational methods to determine whether any could accurately predict the DMS data; per-variant predictions were poor, but per-site predictions were good, with machine learning methods outperforming the physics-based strategy, and ThermoMPNN-D performing most effectively with the RBD and ProteinMPNN with the DD.
Main results
We show NP susceptibility to SEBFF changes varies with region, with mutations to the structured RNA-binding domain (RBD) and dimerization domain (DD) being more likely to cause decreases in SEBFF. We show that the R203K mutation in the linker region increases the folding fitness of NP, suggesting thermostability may have been one factor driving the adoption of the R203K/G204R set of mutations arising in the alpha, gamma and omicron lineages.
Interpretation and novelty
Our DMS results appear consistent with the limited recombinant protein and biophysical data for NP variants available from the literature.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings provide insights into the functional impact of mutations in the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, which may inform surveillance strategies and understanding of viral evolution.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is limited to in vitro deep mutational scanning and computational predictions, with no direct validation in viral replication systems. The evidence strength is moderate due to the comprehensive mutational coverage but lack of in vivo confirmation.

Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive

Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive
作者： David Fitz-Patrick, Omair Sahgal, Leon F. Fouche, Essack Mitha, Mookho Malahleha, Juleen Gayed, Georgina Keep, Ying Zhang, Kayvon Modjarrad, Todd Belanger
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
本研究旨在评估 BA.1 适应的 BNT162b2 疫苗 在之前接种过 BNT162b2 疫苗或未接种过 疫苗 的个体中的免疫原性、耐受性和安全性,解决针对循环变异的更新 疫苗 的需求。
设计与对象
在 18 至 55 岁健康人群中进行了一项 3 期主研究,分为三组 队列研究:之前接种过 BNT162b2 疫苗的人 (队列研究 1-2) 和未接种过 疫苗 的人 (队列研究 3)。
核心方法
通过中和滴度和血清反应百分比的几何平均比(GMR)评估免疫原性,同时监测反应原性和不良事件频率。
主要结果
共有 1471 名参与者参与其中。在队列研究 1中,与一剂BNT162b2相比,一剂或两剂BNT162b2-BA.1后的GMR分别为2.87和2.64。一剂和两剂 BNT162b2-BA.1 的血清反应差异分别为 29.0% 和 21.0%。
解释与创新
结果表明,与原始 疫苗 相比,BNT162b2-BA.1 诱导了更高的中和滴度和更高的血清反应率,表明其具有改善 疫苗 对抗 Omicron BA.1 变体的潜力。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现表明,适应 BA.1 的 疫苗 可以增强对新兴变体的保护,支持其在加强活动中的使用,并为未来的 疫苗 开发策略提供信息。
局限与证据强度
该研究仅限于 18-55 岁的个体,证据基于免疫原性测量而不是临床结果,这可能会影响结果的普遍性。

Immunogenicity, Tolerability, and Safety of BA.1-Adapted BNT162b2 Vaccine in 18- to 55-Year-Olds Previously Vaccinated with BNT162b2 or Who Were COVID-19 Vaccine-Naive

Authors: David Fitz-Patrick, Omair Sahgal, Leon F. Fouche, Essack Mitha, Mookho Malahleha, Juleen Gayed, Georgina Keep, Ying Zhang, Kayvon Modjarrad, Todd Belanger
Original abstract (English)
INTRODUCTION: Variant-adapted COVID-19 vaccines can induce more robust immune responses against closely matched circulating variants than original vaccines. METHODS: Within a phase 3 master study, monovalent Omicron BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 (BNT162b2-BA.1) was evaluated in healthy BNT162b2-experienced (cohorts 1-2) or COVID-19 vaccine-naive (cohort 3) 18 to 55 year-olds. Primary immunogenicity endpoints in cohort 1 were geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of Omicron BA.1 neutralizing titers 1 month after BNT162b2-BA.1 to those after one BNT162b2 dose and differences in percentages of participants with Omicron BA.1 seroresponse between BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2. In cohort 2, primary immunogenicity objectives (participants without evidence of previous SARS-CoV-2 infection) were to demonstrate superiority (GMR two-sided 95% CI lower limit > 1) with respect to neutralizing titer levels and noninferiority with respect to seroresponse difference (difference two-sided 95% CI lower limit > - 5%) for BNT162b2-BA.1 versus BNT162b2. In cohort 3, primary immunogenicity objectives were to demonstrate superiority with respect to neutralizing titer levels and noninferiority with respect to seroresponse after two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses compared with participants receiving BNT162b2 in an efficacy trial. Reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were determined. RESULTS: A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1 (BNT162b2-experienced), GMRs compared with one BNT162b2 dose were 2.87 and 2.64 after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively, and differences in percentages of participants with seroresponse between BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2 were 29.0% and 21.0% for one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses. In cohort 2 (BNT162b2-experienced), one BNT162b2-BA.1 dose met prespecified superiority and noninferiority criteria with respect to GMR and difference in percentage of participants achieving seroresponse, respectively, compared with BNT162b2. In cohort 3 (COVID-19 vaccine-naive), superiority with respect to GMR and noninferiority with respect to difference in percentage of participants achieving seroresponse of BNT162b2-BA.1 to BNT162b2 were met. BNT162b2-BA.1 and BNT162b2 safety and tolerability profiles were similar. CONCLUSIONS: Omicron BA.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccines can broaden immune responses against Omicron BA.1 SARS-CoV-2 variants. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier, NCT04955626.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity, tolerability, and safety of a BA.1-adapted BNT162b2 vaccine in individuals previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 or who were vaccine-naive, addressing the need for updated vaccines against circulating variants.
Design and population
A phase 3 master study was conducted in healthy 18- to 55-year-olds, divided into three cohorts: those previously vaccinated with BNT162b2 (cohorts 1-2) and those who were vaccine-naive (cohort 3).
Core methods
Immunogenicity was assessed through geometric mean ratios (GMRs) of neutralizing titers and seroresponse percentages, while reactogenicity and adverse event frequencies were monitored.
Main results
A total of 1471 participants were included. In cohort 1, GMRs after one or two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses were 2.87 and 2.64, respectively, compared with one BNT162b2 dose. Seroresponse differences were 29.0% and 21.0% for one and two BNT162b2-BA.1 doses, respectively.
Interpretation and novelty
The results demonstrated that BNT162b2-BA.1 induced higher neutralizing titers and greater seroresponse rates compared to the original vaccine, indicating its potential to improve immune responses against the Omicron BA.1 variant.
Scientific and public-health significance
These findings suggest that BA.1-adapted vaccines may enhance protection against emerging variants, supporting their use in booster campaigns and informing future vaccine development strategies.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study was limited to individuals aged 18-55 years, and the evidence is based on immunogenicity measures rather than clinical outcomes, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 Omicron 亚系的 RBD 靶向纳米抗体进行计算优先级排序,然后进行合理的双互补位设计和有针对性的实验验证。

Computational prioritization of RBD-targeting nanobodies across SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages, followed by rational biparatopic design and targeted experimental validation.
作者： Mohammad Mahdi Babashamsi, Kowsar Bagherzadeh, Mohammad Hosseininejad-Chafi, Fatemeh Kazemi-Lomedasht, Mir Salar Kazemi, Hadi Parsian, Mahdi Behdani
摘要中文翻译严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的正在进行的 进化,特别是含有广泛 RBD 突变 的 Omicron 亚系,损害了许多现有中和纳米体的有效性。在这里,我们提出了一个集成的计算实验框架,以优先考虑在突变 RBD 背景下具有有利预测相互作用特征的纳米抗体,并探索其双互补位工程的潜力。通过计算筛选了蛋白质数据库中的 32 种纳米抗体-RBD 复合物,涵盖 8 个 Omicron 亚系 (BA.1-XBB.1.5)。然后,使用分子模拟和在三个生物重复中进行的常规病毒中和测试(cVNT),针对武汉参考毒株和 XBB.1.5(实验室测试开始时的主要亚系)对选定的纳米抗体进行了进一步评估。这些分析确定了 MR17 和 Sb14 的优先顺序。在随后的 cVNT 测定中,MR17 对 XBB.1.5 的中和滴度显着高于对武汉参考菌株的中和滴度,而 Sb14 对两个靶标的滴度相当。双互补位 Sb14-MR17 构建体表现出比任一单体纳米抗体显着更高的针对 XBB.1.5 的中和滴度。此外,还对所选候选药物与新兴 NB.1.8.1 RBD 的相互作用进行了计算评估。总的来说,这些结果强调了多亚系计算分类以及有针对性的实验验证,作为在持续的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗原漂移下优先考虑纳米抗体候选者的实用策略。

严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的正在进行的 进化,特别是含有广泛 RBD 突变 的 Omicron 亚系,损害了许多现有中和纳米体的有效性。

通过计算筛选了蛋白质数据库中的 32 种纳米抗体-RBD 复合物,涵盖 8 个 Omicron 亚系 (BA.1-XBB.1.5)。然后,使用分子模拟和在三个生物重复中进行的常规病毒中和测试(cVNT),针对武汉参考毒株和 XBB.1.5 进一步评估选定的纳米抗体。
主要结果
这些分析确定了 MR17 和 Sb14 的优先顺序。在随后的 cVNT 测定中,MR17 对 XBB.1.5 的中和滴度显着高于对武汉参考菌株的中和滴度,而 Sb14 对两个靶标的滴度相当。双互补位 Sb14-MR17 构建体表现出比任一单体纳米抗体显着更高的针对 XBB.1.5 的中和滴度。
解释与创新
总的来说,这些结果强调了多亚系计算分类以及有针对性的实验验证,作为在持续的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 抗原漂移下优先考虑纳米抗体候选者的实用策略。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现证明了双互补位纳米抗体构建体增强对不断发展的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的中和作用的潜力,为开发针对当前和未来 Omicron 亚谱系的更有效疗法提供了一种有前途的方法。
局限与证据强度
该研究是在体外使用计算预测进行的,并且仅限于特定的纳米抗体候选物和病毒亚谱系,这可能会限制研究结果对所有潜在变异或治疗背景的普遍性。

Computational prioritization of RBD-targeting nanobodies across SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages, followed by rational biparatopic design and targeted experimental validation.

Authors: Mohammad Mahdi Babashamsi, Kowsar Bagherzadeh, Mohammad Hosseininejad-Chafi, Fatemeh Kazemi-Lomedasht, Mir Salar Kazemi, Hadi Parsian, Mahdi Behdani
Original abstract (English)
The ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2, particularly Omicron sublineages harboring extensive RBD mutations, compromises the effectiveness of many existing neutralizing nanobodies. Here, we present an integrated computational-experimental framework to prioritize nanobodies with favorable predicted interaction profiles across mutated RBD backgrounds and to explore their potential for biparatopic engineering. Thirty-two nanobody-RBD complexes from the Protein Data Bank were computationally screened across eight Omicron sublineages (BA.1-XBB.1.5). Selected nanobodies were then further evaluated against the Wuhan reference strain and XBB.1.5-the predominant sublineage at the onset of laboratory testing-using molecular simulations and conventional virus neutralization tests (cVNTs) performed in three biological replicates. These analyses led to the prioritization of MR17 and Sb14. In subsequent cVNT assays, MR17 showed a significantly higher neutralization titer against XBB.1.5 than against the Wuhan reference strain, whereas Sb14 showed comparable titers against both targets. A biparatopic Sb14-MR17 construct exhibited a significantly higher neutralization titer against XBB.1.5 than either monomeric nanobody. In addition, the interaction profiles of selected candidates with the emerging NB.1.8.1 RBD were evaluated computationally. Collectively, these results highlight multi-sublineage computational triage, together with targeted experimental validation, as a practical strategy for prioritizing nanobody candidates under ongoing SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift.

Question and background
The ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2, particularly Omicron sublineages harboring extensive RBD mutations, compromises the effectiveness of many existing neutralizing nanobodies.
Design and population
Here, we present an integrated computational-experimental framework to prioritize nanobodies with favorable predicted interaction profiles across mutated RBD backgrounds and to explore their potential for biparatopic engineering.
Core methods
Thirty-two nanobody-RBD complexes from the Protein Data Bank were computationally screened across eight Omicron sublineages (BA.1-XBB.1.5). Selected nanobodies were then further evaluated against the Wuhan reference strain and XBB.1.5 using molecular simulations and conventional virus neutralization tests (cVNTs) performed in three biological replicates.
Main results
These analyses led to the prioritization of MR17 and Sb14. In subsequent cVNT assays, MR17 showed a significantly higher neutralization titer against XBB.1.5 than against the Wuhan reference strain, whereas Sb14 showed comparable titers against both targets. A biparatopic Sb14-MR17 construct exhibited a significantly higher neutralization titer against XBB.1.5 than either monomeric nanobody.
Interpretation and novelty
Collectively, these results highlight multi-sublineage computational triage, together with targeted experimental validation, as a practical strategy for prioritizing nanobody candidates under ongoing SARS-CoV-2 antigenic drift.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings demonstrate the potential of biparatopic nanobody constructs to enhance neutralization against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants, providing a promising approach for developing more effective therapeutics against current and future Omicron sublineages.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study was conducted in vitro using computational predictions and limited to specific nanobody candidates and viral sublineages, which may limit the generalizability of the findings to all potential variants or therapeutic contexts.

Effects of COVID-19 Control Policies on Malaria Surveillance: A Comparative Analysis of North and South Korea.

Effects of COVID-19 Control Policies on Malaria Surveillance: A Comparative Analysis of North and South Korea.
作者： Jong-Hun Kim, Jisun Sung
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
The study investigates why malaria cases increased during the COVID-19 response in North and South Korea, despite both countries being identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having the potential to eliminate malaria.
设计与对象
This comparative analysis examined epidemiological, entomological, and meteorological data from national and international surveillance systems in North and South Korea during the period of the COVID-19 response.
核心方法
该研究利用世界卫生组织的分析框架来评估疟疾死灰复燃的驱动因素,分析两国的检测可用性、响应时间和确诊病例的数据。
主要结果
In North Korea, border closures led to a 90% reduction in malaria testing by 2021, while confirmed cases rose from 1819 in 2020 to 3160 in 2023. In South Korea, public health resources were diverted to COVID-19, weakening malaria control activities. Relapse cases increased from zero in 2021 to eight in 2023, and confirmed cases rose from 274 in 2021 to 673 in 2023.
解释与创新
The authors interpret that disruptions caused by the COVID-19 response, such as supply chain failures and resource diversion, were the main drivers of the observed malaria resurgence, with no meaningful changes in the biological factors like vector density or drug resistance.
科研与公卫意义
研究结果强调了在突发公共卫生事件期间维持疟疾 监测 和控制工作的重要性,因为资源转移和后勤挑战可能会严重影响疾病管理。
局限与证据强度
该研究仅限于抽象级别的数据,证据基于报告的检测可用性和响应时间的变化,这可能无法完全反映疟疾卷土重来的复杂性。证据强度中等。

Effects of COVID-19 Control Policies on Malaria Surveillance: A Comparative Analysis of North and South Korea.

Authors: Jong-Hun Kim, Jisun Sung
Original abstract (English)
PURPOSE: Both South and North Korea are identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having the potential to eliminate malaria. However, the increase in malaria cases during the COVID-19 response has prompted an investigation into the reasons behind this unexpected rise. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Epidemiological, entomological, and meteorological data from national and international surveillance systems were analyzed. Using the WHO's analytical framework, which can be effectively applied during the elimination phase, we assessed drivers of malaria resurgence in North and South Korea. RESULTS: In North Korea, border closures caused a severe shortage of rapid diagnostic test kits, reducing malaria testing by over 90% by 2021. Microscopy use increased but remained insufficient, while confirmed cases rose from 1819 in 2020 to 3160 in 2023. In South Korea, public health resources were diverted to COVID-19, weakening malaria control activities. The response time for epidemiological investigations increased from 1.3 days in 2019 to 4.3 days in 2021. Relapse cases, which were zero in 2021, increased to eight in 2023, and confirmed cases rose from 274 in 2021 to 673 in 2023. There were no meaningful changes in the drivers of malaria resurgence, including importation of malaria parasites or human susceptibility. With no notable shifts in vector density, variations in temperature and precipitation did not explain the rise in either country, and there were no reports of emerging resistance to insecticides or antimalarial drugs. CONCLUSION: These COVID-19-related disruptions, including supply chain failures and the diversion of human resources, impaired malaria control in countries on the Korean Peninsula.

Question and background
The study investigates why malaria cases increased during the COVID-19 response in North and South Korea, despite both countries being identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having the potential to eliminate malaria.
Design and population
This comparative analysis examined epidemiological, entomological, and meteorological data from national and international surveillance systems in North and South Korea during the period of the COVID-19 response.
Core methods
The study used the WHO's analytical framework to assess drivers of malaria resurgence, analyzing data on testing availability, response times, and confirmed cases in both countries.
Main results
In North Korea, border closures led to a 90% reduction in malaria testing by 2021, while confirmed cases rose from 1819 in 2020 to 3160 in 2023. In South Korea, public health resources were diverted to COVID-19, weakening malaria control activities. Relapse cases increased from zero in 2021 to eight in 2023, and confirmed cases rose from 274 in 2021 to 673 in 2023.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpret that disruptions caused by the COVID-19 response, such as supply chain failures and resource diversion, were the main drivers of the observed malaria resurgence, with no meaningful changes in the biological factors like vector density or drug resistance.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings highlight the importance of maintaining malaria surveillance and control efforts during public health emergencies, as resource diversion and logistical challenges can significantly impact disease management.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is limited to abstract-level data, and the evidence is based on reported changes in testing availability and response times, which may not fully capture the complexity of malaria resurgence. The evidence strength is moderate.

JN.1 适应的 疫苗接种 与祖先记忆 B 细胞在 JN.1 抗原空间内的中和作用的重新调整有关

JN.1-adapted vaccination is associated with readjustment of ancestral memory B cells toward neutralization within the JN.1 antigenic space
作者： Metodi V. Stankov, Matthias Bruhn, Markus Hoffmann, Abdus Salam, Amy Eichmann, Inga Nehlmeier, Luis A. Manthey, Torsten Witte, Stefan Pöhlmann, Gerrit Ahrenstorf
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
The antigenic drift of SARS-CoV-2 toward the JN.1 lineage has prompted the development of variant-adapted COVID-19 booster vaccines, but concerns exist about their ability to realign the immune response in highly pre-exposed populations.
设计与对象
We analyzed antibody and B cell responses in pre-exposed individuals (n = 42; median 4.5 prior COVID-19 vaccinations; 90% with at least one prior SARS-CoV-2 infection) following vaccination with a JN.1-adapted mRNA vaccine.
核心方法
对代表性子 队列研究 (n = 7) 中的抗原特异性记忆 B 细胞进行单细胞 RNA 测序,并结合功能性单克隆抗体分析,以评估体细胞超突变和中和能力。
主要结果
疫苗接种 与 IgG 结合增加以及 JN.1 和相关后代变体的中和增强相关,纵向分析显示第 21 天时仅 JN.1 的记忆 B 细胞适度增加。
解释与创新
研究结果表明,预先存在的类别转换记忆 B 细胞已成熟,而不是大量从头招募初始 B 细胞,这证明了 免疫应答 向 JN.1 抗原空间的改进。
科研与公卫意义
JN.1适应的增强剂疫苗接种有效地完善了预先存在的记忆B细胞库,增强了当代和抗原性邻近变体的中和,这为疫苗进化严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体的策略提供了信息。
局限与证据强度
证据强度中等,因为该研究是在小型 队列研究 (n = 42) 和子 队列研究 (n = 7) 中进行的单细胞测序,限制了普遍性。

JN.1-adapted vaccination is associated with readjustment of ancestral memory B cells toward neutralization within the JN.1 antigenic space

Authors: Metodi V. Stankov, Matthias Bruhn, Markus Hoffmann, Abdus Salam, Amy Eichmann, Inga Nehlmeier, Luis A. Manthey, Torsten Witte, Stefan Pöhlmann, Gerrit Ahrenstorf
Original abstract (English)
The antigenic drift of SARS-CoV-2 toward the JN.1 lineage has prompted the development of variant-adapted COVID-19 booster vaccines. However, these boosters are thought to primarily recall pre-existing memory B cells (MBC), raising concerns about their ability to realign the immune response in highly pre-exposed populations. Here we analyze antibody and B cell responses in pre-exposed individuals (n = 42; median 4.5 prior COVID-19 vaccinations; 90% with at least one prior SARS-CoV-2 infection) following vaccination with a JN.1-adapted mRNA vaccine. Vaccination is associated with increased IgG binding and enhanced neutralization of JN.1 and related descendant variants. Longitudinal profiling of antigen-specific MBC shows that Wu01-only and Wu01/JN.1 cross-reactive cells remain dominant, while JN.1-only cells modestly increase by day 21. Single-cell RNA-sequencing of antigen-specific MBC in a representative sub-cohort (n = 7), combined with functional monoclonal antibody analyses, demonstrates that somatic hypermutation (SHM) drives intra-clonotype specialization toward improved JN.1 binding and neutralization. These findings indicate maturation of pre-existing, class-switched MBC rather than substantial de novo recruitment of naïve B cells. In conclusion, JN.1-adapted booster vaccination is associated with refinement of pre-existing MBC repertoires toward the JN.1 antigenic space and with enhanced neutralization of contemporary and antigenically proximate variants.

Question and background
The antigenic drift of SARS-CoV-2 toward the JN.1 lineage has prompted the development of variant-adapted COVID-19 booster vaccines, but concerns exist about their ability to realign the immune response in highly pre-exposed populations.
Design and population
We analyzed antibody and B cell responses in pre-exposed individuals (n = 42; median 4.5 prior COVID-19 vaccinations; 90% with at least one prior SARS-CoV-2 infection) following vaccination with a JN.1-adapted mRNA vaccine.
Core methods
Single-cell RNA-sequencing of antigen-specific memory B cells in a representative sub-cohort (n = 7), combined with functional monoclonal antibody analyses, was performed to assess somatic hypermutation and neutralization capabilities.
Main results
Vaccination is associated with increased IgG binding and enhanced neutralization of JN.1 and related descendant variants, with longitudinal profiling showing modest increases in JN.1-only memory B cells by day 21.
Interpretation and novelty
The findings indicate maturation of pre-existing, class-switched memory B cells rather than substantial de novo recruitment of naïve B cells, demonstrating refinement of the immune response toward the JN.1 antigenic space.
Scientific and public-health significance
JN.1-adapted booster vaccination effectively refines pre-existing memory B cell repertoires, enhancing neutralization of contemporary and antigenically proximate variants, which informs vaccine strategies for evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.
Limitations and evidence strength
The evidence strength is moderate, as the study was conducted in a small cohort (n = 42) with a sub-cohort (n = 7) for single-cell sequencing, limiting generalizability.
