Detecting and supporting COVID-19 outbreak response in a small-scale nursing home through passive wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2

Detecting and supporting COVID-19 outbreak response in a small-scale nursing home through passive wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2
作者： Min Ki Jeon, Doris Yoong Wen Di, Maria Steadmon, Stella Maris Remigio, Pamela O'Brien, Daniel P. Strange, Vila Chanthasouvanh, Dayna Ornellas, Edward Desmond, Tao Yan
摘要中文翻译摘要:被动废水采样已成为病原体监测的一种经济有效的方法,但在极小规模人群中的应用尚未得到充分研究。本研究报告了在拥有24名居民的小型养老院中使用棉签作为被动采样器检测呼吸道病毒(包括严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、甲型流感、乙型流感和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV))。通过逆转录数字PCR(RT-dPCR)对废水进行为期1年的每周监测,结果在连续4周内检测到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2聚集。当废水中的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2浓度在第三和第四周达到较高水平时,全基因组测序实现了>98%的基因组覆盖,确定了LB.1.5谱系,而低浓度样本仅产生部分基因组。在第四周出现临床症状时启动了临床检测,确认24名居民和工作人员中有15人感染严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2。临床样本测序确认11例为LB.1.5,证实了废水检测结果。通过靶向富集测序在废水中还额外检测到甲型流感亚型H3N2和H1N1,RT-dPCR检测到一次RSV,这些均与已确认的临床病例无关。这些结果表明废水监测可以在临床症状出现前进行早期检测,使用棉签的被动采样是小型设施中暴发监测的一种实用且敏感的策略。研究还强调了需要明确的应对方案,包括当废水病毒浓度超过定义阈值时进行快速临床检测和队列隔离措施。重要性:养老院是传染病暴发风险最高的场所之一,但由于无症状感染率高和常规临床监测资源有限,早期检测仍然具有挑战性。本研究证明,基于棉签的低成本被动废水采样器可以在仅有24名居民的养老院中提前3周检测到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,这是该方法得到验证的最小规模人群。废水衍生的基因组质量与临床测序相匹配,能够识别夏威夷地区的新型严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2谱系。这些发现支持将被动废水监测作为小型集体护理设施的实用早期预警工具,前提是制定了明确的机构应对方案。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
被动废水采样已成为病原体监测的一种经济有效的方法,但在极小规模人群中的应用尚未得到充分研究。养老院是传染病暴发风险最高的场所之一,但由于无症状感染率高和常规临床监测资源有限,早期检测仍然具有挑战性。
设计与对象
本研究报告了在拥有 24 名居民的小型疗养院中使用卫生棉条作为被动采样器来检测呼吸道病毒,包括 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2、甲型流感、乙型流感和呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)。
核心方法
通过逆转录数字PCR(RT-dPCR)对废水进行为期1年的每周监测,结果在连续4周内检测到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2聚集。当废水中的严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2浓度在第三和第四周达到较高水平时,全基因组测序实现了>98%的基因组覆盖,确定了LB.1.5谱系,而低浓度样本仅产生部分基因组。
主要结果
第四周开始临床测试,当时也出现了临床症状,并确认 24 名住院医师和工作人员中有 15 人感染了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2。临床样本测序证实了 11 例中存在 LB.1.5,证实了废水检测结果。
解释与创新
这些结果表明,废水 暴发 可以先于临床症状进行早期检测,并且使用卫生棉条进行被动采样是小型设施中 暴发 暴发 暴发 的实用且敏感的策略。该研究还强调需要制定明确的应对方案,包括当废水病毒浓度超过规定阈值时进行快速临床测试和分组措施。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现支持被动废水 监测 作为小型聚集护理设施的实用早期预警工具,前提是制定明确的机构应对方案。这项研究表明,廉价的基于卫生棉条的被动废水采样器可以在只有 24 名居民的疗养院出现临床症状之前长达 3 周检测到 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2,这是该方法已得到验证的最小人群。
局限与证据强度
所提供的证据未报告具体限制或证据强度评估。然而,该研究表明,废水来源的 基因组 符合临床测序质量,从而能够鉴定夏威夷新的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 谱系。

Detecting and supporting COVID-19 outbreak response in a small-scale nursing home through passive wastewater surveillance of SARS-CoV-2

Authors: Min Ki Jeon, Doris Yoong Wen Di, Maria Steadmon, Stella Maris Remigio, Pamela O'Brien, Daniel P. Strange, Vila Chanthasouvanh, Dayna Ornellas, Edward Desmond, Tao Yan
Original abstract (English)
ABSTRACT Passive wastewater sampling has emerged as a cost-effective approach for pathogen monitoring, but its application in very small populations has not been well studied. This study reports the use of tampons as passive samplers in a small-scale nursing home of 24 residents to detect respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Weekly wastewater surveillance by reverse transcription digital PCR (RT-dPCR) for a 1-year period resulted in a cluster of consecutive SARS-CoV-2 detections over 4 weeks. When wastewater SARS-CoV-2 concentrations reached higher levels in the third and fourth weeks, whole-genome sequencing achieved >98% genome coverage, identifying lineage LB.1.5, while lower-concentration samples produced only partial genomes. Clinical testing was initiated in the fourth week when clinical symptoms also emerged, and confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in 15 of 24 residents and staff. Sequencing of the clinical samples confirmed LB.1.5 in 11 cases, corroborating the wastewater findings. Influenza A subtypes H3N2 and H1N1 were additionally detected in wastewater by targeted enrichment sequencing, and RSV was detected once by RT-dPCR, neither of which was associated with confirmed clinical cases. These results demonstrate that wastewater surveillance can precede clinical symptoms for early detection, and passive sampling using tampons is a practical and sensitive strategy for outbreak surveillance in small-scale facilities. The study also highlights the need for clear response protocols that include rapid clinical testing and cohorting measures when wastewater viral concentrations exceed defined thresholds. IMPORTANCE Nursing homes are among the highest-risk settings for infectious disease outbreaks, yet early detection remains challenging due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections and limited resources for routine clinical surveillance. This study demonstrates that inexpensive tampon-based passive wastewater samplers can detect SARS-CoV-2 up to 3 weeks before clinical symptoms emerge in a nursing home with only 24 residents, which is the smallest population in which this method has been validated. Wastewater-derived genomes matched clinical sequencing quality, enabling identification of a novel SARS-CoV-2 lineage new to Hawai'i. These findings support passive wastewater surveillance as a practical early warning tool for small congregate care facilities, provided that clear institutional response protocols are in place.

Question and background
Passive wastewater sampling has emerged as a cost-effective approach for pathogen monitoring, but its application in very small populations has not been well studied. Nursing homes are among the highest-risk settings for infectious disease outbreaks, yet early detection remains challenging due to the high prevalence of asymptomatic infections and limited resources for routine clinical surveillance.
Design and population
This study reports the use of tampons as passive samplers in a small-scale nursing home of 24 residents to detect respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
Core methods
Weekly wastewater surveillance by reverse transcription digital PCR (RT-dPCR) for a 1-year period resulted in a cluster of consecutive SARS-CoV-2 detections over 4 weeks. When wastewater SARS-CoV-2 concentrations reached higher levels in the third and fourth weeks, whole-genome sequencing achieved >98% genome coverage, identifying lineage LB.1.5, while lower-concentration samples produced only partial genomes.
Main results
Clinical testing was initiated in the fourth week when clinical symptoms also emerged, and confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in 15 of 24 residents and staff. Sequencing of the clinical samples confirmed LB.1.5 in 11 cases, corroborating the wastewater findings.
Interpretation and novelty
These results demonstrate that wastewater surveillance can precede clinical symptoms for early detection, and passive sampling using tampons is a practical and sensitive strategy for outbreak surveillance in small-scale facilities. The study also highlights the need for clear response protocols that include rapid clinical testing and cohorting measures when wastewater viral concentrations exceed defined thresholds.
Scientific and public-health significance
These findings support passive wastewater surveillance as a practical early warning tool for small congregate care facilities, provided that clear institutional response protocols are in place. This study demonstrates that inexpensive tampon-based passive wastewater samplers can detect SARS-CoV-2 up to 3 weeks before clinical symptoms emerge in a nursing home with only 24 residents, which is the smallest population in which this method has been validated.
Limitations and evidence strength
The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment. However, the study demonstrates that wastewater-derived genomes matched clinical sequencing quality, enabling identification of a novel SARS-CoV-2 lineage new to Hawai'i.

A Novel Older-Adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index to Measure the Transition from Pandemic Mortality to Endemic Resilience in Spain

A Novel Older-Adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index to Measure the Transition from Pandemic Mortality to Endemic Resilience in Spain
作者： Elena Moreno-Guillamont, Carmen I. Sáez-Lleó, María Auxiliadora Dea-Ayuela, Jose M. Soriano, María Auxiliadora Dea‐Ayuela
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
The COVID-19 pandemic produced a severe and heterogeneous burden across age groups, territories and epidemic phases in Spain, with older adults experiencing disproportionately high rates of hospitalization, intensive care unit admission and death, particularly during early waves when vaccination was unavailable.
设计与对象
This study developed and applied a novel Older-adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index (O-CSDI) to weekly COVID-19 surveillance data from the 17 Spanish autonomous communities and the two autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla, covering January 2020 to July 2023 with 3496 autonomous community–week observations and 143 variables from four open-access surveillance sources.
核心方法
The O-CSDI quantifies the degree to which reported COVID-19 incidence became disconnected from hospitalization, ICU admission and mortality in adults aged 60–69, 70–79 and ≥80 years, with the primary version based on the death-to-case ratio and complementary versions examining hospitalization-to-case, ICU-to-hospitalization and death-to-hospitalization transitions.
主要结果
结果显示,各个阶段、地域单位和年龄层之间存在渐进但异质的脱钩,其中在 Omicron BA.1/BA.2 期间观察到最强的脱钩,并且在年龄≥80 岁的成年人中残余 死亡率 负担最高。
解释与创新
作者将这些发现解释为生态的描述性指标,而不是个体层面的风险或因果估计,为回顾性大流行评估和老龄化人口的防范提供了可重复的流行病学工具。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现为回顾性大流行评估和老龄化人口的防备提供了可重复的流行病学工具,为从大流行 死亡率 到地方病恢复力的转变提供了见解。
局限与证据强度
基于 发病率 和比率的 O-CSDI 分析仅限于 2020 年 3 月至 2022 年 3 月,因为在过渡到简化的 监测 后,开放获取的单个事件计数在结构上不再具有可比性,并且由于数据的生态性质和时间限制,证据强度被评估为中等。

A Novel Older-Adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index to Measure the Transition from Pandemic Mortality to Endemic Resilience in Spain

Authors: Elena Moreno-Guillamont, Carmen I. Sáez-Lleó, María Auxiliadora Dea-Ayuela, Jose M. Soriano, María Auxiliadora Dea‐Ayuela
Original abstract (English)
The COVID-19 pandemic produced a severe and heterogeneous burden across age groups, territories and epidemic phases in Spain. Older adults experienced disproportionately high rates of hospitalization, intensive care unit (ICU) admission and death, particularly during the early pandemic waves when vaccination was unavailable. However, the relationship between surveillance-confirmed cases and severe outcomes changed substantially over time, a phenomenon termed epidemiological decoupling. This study developed and applied a novel Older-adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index (O-CSDI) to weekly COVID-19 surveillance data from the 17 Spanish autonomous communities and the two autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla. The integrated dataset covered January 2020 to July 2023 and comprised 3496 autonomous community–week observations and 143 variables obtained from four open-access surveillance sources: ISCIII-RENAVE, Datadista/Ministerio de Sanidad, Our World in Data and the MoMo excess mortality system. However, the primary incidence- and ratio-based O-CSDI analyses were restricted to March 2020–March 2022 because open-access individual event counts were no longer structurally comparable after the transition to reduced surveillance. Data from later periods were retained only for contextual vaccination and MoMo mortality indicators. The O-CSDI quantifies the degree to which reported COVID-19 incidence became disconnected from hospitalization, ICU admission and mortality in adults aged 60–69, 70–79 and ≥80 years. The primary version of the index was based on the death-to-case ratio, while complementary versions examined hospitalization-to-case, ICU-to-hospitalization and death-to-hospitalization transitions. Results showed progressive but heterogeneous decoupling across phases, territorial units and age strata, with the strongest decoupling observed during the Omicron BA.1/BA.2 period and the highest residual mortality burden in adults aged ≥80 years. All results were interpreted as ecological, descriptive indicators rather than individual-level risks or causal estimates. These findings provide a reproducible epidemiological tool for retrospective pandemic evaluation and preparedness in ageing populations.

Question and background
The COVID-19 pandemic produced a severe and heterogeneous burden across age groups, territories and epidemic phases in Spain, with older adults experiencing disproportionately high rates of hospitalization, intensive care unit admission and death, particularly during early waves when vaccination was unavailable.
Design and population
This study developed and applied a novel Older-adult COVID-19 Severity Decoupling Index (O-CSDI) to weekly COVID-19 surveillance data from the 17 Spanish autonomous communities and the two autonomous cities of Ceuta and Melilla, covering January 2020 to July 2023 with 3496 autonomous community–week observations and 143 variables from four open-access surveillance sources.
Core methods
The O-CSDI quantifies the degree to which reported COVID-19 incidence became disconnected from hospitalization, ICU admission and mortality in adults aged 60–69, 70–79 and ≥80 years, with the primary version based on the death-to-case ratio and complementary versions examining hospitalization-to-case, ICU-to-hospitalization and death-to-hospitalization transitions.
Main results
Results showed progressive but heterogeneous decoupling across phases, territorial units and age strata, with the strongest decoupling observed during the Omicron BA.1/BA.2 period and the highest residual mortality burden in adults aged ≥80 years.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpreted these findings as ecological, descriptive indicators rather than individual-level risks or causal estimates, providing a reproducible epidemiological tool for retrospective pandemic evaluation and preparedness in ageing populations.
Scientific and public-health significance
These findings provide a reproducible epidemiological tool for retrospective pandemic evaluation and preparedness in ageing populations, offering insights into the transition from pandemic mortality to endemic resilience.
Limitations and evidence strength
The primary incidence- and ratio-based O-CSDI analyses were restricted to March 2020–March 2022 because open-access individual event counts were no longer structurally comparable after the transition to reduced surveillance, with evidence strength assessed as moderate due to the ecological nature of the data and temporal limitations.

上皮细胞中 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的纳米管介导的细胞间扩散揭示了 宿主 靶向的 抗病毒药物 漏洞。

Tunneling nanotube-mediated intercellular spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants in epithelial cells reveals a host-targeted antiviral vulnerability.
作者： Gurleen Kaur, Ritika Khatri, Varun Kumar, Bharat Lohiya, Akanksha Chauhan, Sweety Samal
摘要中文翻译我们证明,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 利用隧道纳米管 (TNT) 作为上皮细胞中细胞间 传播 的基于肌动蛋白的导管。与祖先的Wuhan-Hu-1和Omicron毒株相比,Delta变种的TNT形成显着增强,这与它们的相对传播性一致。Delta 变体还促进了广泛的丝状伪足和分支 TNT 网络,促进有效的细胞间传播。共聚焦和超微结构分析揭示了线粒体和溶酶体通过这些纳米管的主动转移,表明 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 与 宿主 细胞器运输一起支持复制和持久性。Cdc42 依赖性肌动蛋白重塑或 CaMKII 信号传导的药理学抑制会破坏 TNT 形成。总的来说,这些发现将 TNT 确定为上皮细胞中变异依赖性 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 传播的关键途径,并揭示 宿主 细胞骨架动力学作为限制病毒传播的易处理的 抗病毒药物 靶点。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
本研究旨在研究 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变异在上皮细胞之间传播的机制,并确定与 宿主 因子相关的潜在 抗病毒药物 靶点。
设计与对象
该研究重点关注严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体,包括Delta、Wuhan-Hu-1和Omicron,并通过实验分析检查它们在上皮细胞中的细胞间扩散。
核心方法
研究人员使用共聚焦和超微结构分析来观察 宿主 细胞器通过隧道纳米管 (TNT) 的转移,并测试了针对 Cdc42 依赖性肌动蛋白重塑和 CaMKII 信号传导的药理学抑制剂。
主要结果
与Wuhan-Hu-1和Omicron相比,Delta变体中TNT的形成显着增强,并且这些纳米管促进了线粒体和溶酶体的转移。
解释与创新
研究结果表明,TNT 是 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 在上皮细胞中传播的关键途径,并强调 宿主 细胞骨架动力学是 抗病毒药物 的潜在靶点。
科研与公卫意义
这些结果提供了对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 传播机制的深入了解,并提出了针对 宿主 因子以限制病毒 传播 的新策略。
局限与证据强度
该研究仅限于体外观察,并未考虑体内条件,但基于直接实验结果的证据是强有力的。

Tunneling nanotube-mediated intercellular spread of SARS-CoV-2 variants in epithelial cells reveals a host-targeted antiviral vulnerability.

Authors: Gurleen Kaur, Ritika Khatri, Varun Kumar, Bharat Lohiya, Akanksha Chauhan, Sweety Samal
Original abstract (English)
We demonstrate that SARS-CoV-2 exploits tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) as actin-based conduits for intercellular transmission in epithelial cells. TNT formation was markedly enhanced in the Delta variant compared with the ancestral Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron strains, consistent with their relative transmissibility. The Delta variant also promoted extensive filopodia and branched TNT networks, facilitating efficient cell-to-cell dissemination. Confocal and ultrastructural analyses revealed active transfer of mitochondria and lysosomes through these nanotubes, indicating that SARS-CoV-2 co-opts host organelle trafficking to support replication and persistence. Pharmacological inhibition of Cdc42-dependent actin remodeling or CaMKII signaling disrupted TNT formation. Collectively, these findings identify TNTs as a crucial pathway for variant-dependent SARS-CoV-2 dissemination in epithelial cells and reveal host cytoskeletal dynamics as a tractable antiviral target for limiting viral spread.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms by which SARS-CoV-2 variants spread between epithelial cells and identify potential antiviral targets related to host factors.
Design and population
The study focused on SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Delta, Wuhan-Hu-1, and Omicron, and examined their intercellular spread in epithelial cells through experimental analysis.
Core methods
The researchers used confocal and ultrastructural analyses to observe the transfer of host organelles through tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) and tested pharmacological inhibitors targeting Cdc42-dependent actin remodeling and CaMKII signaling.
Main results
TNT formation was significantly enhanced in the Delta variant compared to Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron, and these nanotubes facilitated the transfer of mitochondria and lysosomes.
Interpretation and novelty
The findings suggest that TNTs are a critical pathway for SARS-CoV-2 dissemination in epithelial cells and highlight host cytoskeletal dynamics as a potential antiviral target.
Scientific and public-health significance
These results provide insights into the mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 spread and suggest new strategies for targeting host factors to limit viral transmission.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is limited to in vitro observations and does not account for in vivo conditions, but the evidence is strong based on direct experimental findings.

SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae co‐infection during the early COVID‐19 pandemic: diagnostic bias leading to delayed recognition

SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae co‐infection during the early COVID‐19 pandemic: diagnostic bias leading to delayed recognition
作者： Hidehiro Watanabe, Takehito Kobayashi, Yasuyuki Takebayashi, Hideaki Takahashi, Hiroaki Fujita, Yusuke Watanabe, Itaru Nakamura
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
Co‐infections during the early COVID‐19 pandemic were frequently under‐recognized due to diagnostic bias, limited availability of pathogen‐specific testing, and the overwhelming clinical focus on SARS‐CoV‐2.
设计与对象
我们报告了一例 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 和肺炎支原体双重感染病例,患者为一名先前健康的 35 岁男性,他于 2020 年 4 月出现发热性呼吸道疾病。
核心方法
However, when the SARS‐CoV‐2 PCR result was subsequently recognized on day 6 of illness, diagnostic anchoring toward COVID‐19 occurred, and M. pneumoniae was downgraded to a secondary consideration despite supportive radiological and serological evidence.
主要结果
胸部计算机断层扫描显示多个小的毛玻璃样混浊,血清学 显示肺炎支原体 PA 滴度为 1:640,导致临床医生初步诊断肺炎支原体肺炎。
解释与创新
这个案例说明了认知偏差和与大流行相关的诊断限制如何导致大流行早期期间对合并感染的延迟识别。
科研与公卫意义
对诊断陷阱的认识对于准确评估当代呼吸道感染仍然至关重要。
局限与证据强度
相比之下,目前的 Omicron 谱系变异表现出严重程度减弱和确定性较低,使得住院患者的合并感染可能更具临床意义,但很容易被忽视。

SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae co‐infection during the early COVID‐19 pandemic: diagnostic bias leading to delayed recognition

Authors: Hidehiro Watanabe, Takehito Kobayashi, Yasuyuki Takebayashi, Hideaki Takahashi, Hiroaki Fujita, Yusuke Watanabe, Itaru Nakamura
Original abstract (English)
Co‐infections during the early COVID‐19 pandemic were frequently under‐recognized due to diagnostic bias, limited availability of pathogen‐specific testing, and the overwhelming clinical focus on SARS‐CoV‐2. We report a case of co‐infection with SARS‐CoV‐2 and Mycoplasma pneumoniae in a previously healthy 35‐year‐old man who presented with febrile respiratory illness in April 2020. Chest computed tomography demonstrated multiple small ground‐glass opacities, and serology showed a M. pneumoniae PA titer of 1:640, leading clinicians to initially diagnose M. pneumoniae pneumonia. However, when the SARS‐CoV‐2 PCR result was subsequently recognized on day 6 of illness, diagnostic anchoring toward COVID‐19 occurred, and M. pneumoniae was downgraded to a secondary consideration despite supportive radiological and serological evidence. This sequence contributed to premature closure and base‐rate neglect, with co‐infection formally acknowledged only after both results became available. The patient improved with supportive care and appropriate antimicrobial therapy. This case illustrates how cognitive biases and pandemic‐related diagnostic constraints contributed to delayed recognition of co‐infections during the early pandemic. In contrast, current Omicron‐lineage variants exhibit attenuated severity and low ascertainment, making co‐infections in hospitalized patients potentially more clinically significant yet easily overlooked. Awareness of diagnostic pitfalls remains essential for accurate evaluation of respiratory infections in the contemporary era.

严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 疫苗 接受者的概念验证纵向研究中隐藏的无症状突破性感染

Hidden asymptomatic breakthrough infection in a proof-of-concept longitudinal study on SARS-CoV-2 vaccine recipients
作者： Chiaho Shih, You-Zhen Liao, Che-Yu Hsu, Ying-Chen Tsai, Ming-Yen Lin, Hsin-Ying Clair Chiou, Wen-Hui Kuan, Chih-Hsu Chang, An-Ting Liou, Yu‐Chi Chou
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
该研究旨在解决在接种疫苗后人群中识别无症状 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的挑战,因为这些人可能在不知情的情况下传播病毒而不表现出症状。
设计与对象
对 129 名未感染过 疫苗 的接受者进行了一项纵向研究,他们接受了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突 (S) 蛋白 疫苗 平台的各种组合的免疫。该研究的重点是追踪这些个体随时间的抗体反应。
核心方法
在三个时间点收集血清:第一次给药前 (v1)、第三次给药后 2 周 (v7) 和 6 个月 (v8)。通过 ELISA 测量抗核衣壳(抗 N)和抗 S IgG 抗体滴度,并使用活病毒和假病毒测定评估病毒中和活​​性。统计分析验证了一个独特的无症状组,其特征是抗 S ++(中间)/抗 N +(基线)的抗体谱。
主要结果
通过开发迭代系列筛查方法,在未确诊病例中发现了无症状突破性感染。在标准化的 v8 血清中,确诊病例显示抗 S +++(高)/抗 N +++(高)表型,而未感染受试者则显示抗 S +(低)/抗 N +(基线)表型。队列研究 分为三个不同的组:确诊病例 (21%)、无症状突破性感染者 (17%) 和未感染者 (62%)。
解释与创新
该研究的方法通过使用自我匹配的纵向血清样本对来识别接种良好的人群中的无症状突破性感染,从而能够更准确地估计 疫苗 的疗效和感染情况。这是此类鉴定的第一份初步报告。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现可能会更准确地告知已接种疫苗的个体中 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染的 监测 和 诊断,有助于更好地了解 疫苗 的有效性和无症状 传播 的动态。
局限与证据强度
该研究仅限于仅摘要分析,证据基于单个纵向 队列研究。由于摘要中缺乏详细的统计或临床验证,研究结果的可信度中等。

Hidden asymptomatic breakthrough infection in a proof-of-concept longitudinal study on SARS-CoV-2 vaccine recipients

Authors: Chiaho Shih, You-Zhen Liao, Che-Yu Hsu, Ying-Chen Tsai, Ming-Yen Lin, Hsin-Ying Clair Chiou, Wen-Hui Kuan, Chih-Hsu Chang, An-Ting Liou, Yu‐Chi Chou
Original abstract (English)
Abstract Background Individuals with asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection can unknowingly transmit the virus, yet identifying such subclinical infections in post-vaccinated populations remains challenging. Methods We conducted a longitudinal study of 129 infection-naïve vaccine recipients immunized with various combinations of SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) protein vaccine platforms. Sera were collected before the first dose ( v 1), at 2 weeks ( v 7) and 6 months ( v 8) after the third dose. Taiwan’s first major COVID-19 outbreak occurred between v 7 and v 8. We measured anti-nucleocapsid (anti-N) and anti-S IgG antibody titers by ELISA and assessed virus-neutralizing activity using live virus and pseudovirus assays. Results By developing an iterative serial screening method, we identified asymptomatic breakthrough (post-vaccination) infections among unconfirmed cases. Our v 7- v 8 paired cohort resolved into three distinct groups: confirmed cases (21%), asymptomatic breakthrough infections (17%), and uninfected subjects (62%). In normalized v 8 sera, confirmed cases exhibited an anti-S +++ (high) /anti-N +++ (high) phenotype, while uninfected subjects showed an anti-S + (low)/anti-N + (baseline) phenotype. Statistical analysis validated a distinct asymptomatic group characterized by an antibody profile anti-S ++ (intermediate) /anti-N + (baseline). Conclusions This approach may enable more accurate estimates of vaccine efficacy and infection prevalence. In a spike-vaccinated population, anti-N antibody is more a potential specific marker for COVID-19 symptomatic disease than an ideal marker for SARS-CoV-2 infection. To our knowledge, this is the first preliminary report of identification of asymptomatic breakthrough infection from a well-vaccinated population using self-matched longitudinal pairs of serum samples.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study aimed to address the challenge of identifying asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections in post-vaccinated populations, as these individuals can unknowingly transmit the virus without showing symptoms.
Design and population
A longitudinal study was conducted on 129 infection-naïve vaccine recipients who were immunized with various combinations of SARS-CoV-2 spike (S) protein vaccine platforms. The study focused on tracking antibody responses over time in these individuals.
Core methods
Sera were collected at three time points: before the first dose (v1), at 2 weeks (v7) and 6 months (v8) after the third dose. Anti-nucleocapsid (anti-N) and anti-S IgG antibody titers were measured by ELISA, and virus-neutralizing activity was assessed using live virus and pseudovirus assays. Statistical analysis validated a distinct asymptomatic group characterized by an antibody profile of anti-S ++ (intermediate) /anti-N + (baseline).
Main results
By developing an iterative serial screening method, asymptomatic breakthrough infections were identified among unconfirmed cases. In normalized v8 sera, confirmed cases showed an anti-S +++ (high)/anti-N +++ (high) phenotype, while uninfected subjects had an anti-S + (low)/anti-N + (baseline) phenotype. The cohort resolved into three distinct groups: confirmed cases (21%), asymptomatic breakthrough infections (17%), and uninfected subjects (62%).
Interpretation and novelty
The study's approach enabled more accurate estimates of vaccine efficacy and infection prevalence by identifying asymptomatic breakthrough infections in a well-vaccinated population using self-matched longitudinal pairs of serum samples. This is the first preliminary report of such identification.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings may inform more precise surveillance and diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infections in vaccinated individuals, contributing to better understanding of vaccine effectiveness and the dynamics of asymptomatic transmission.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is limited to an abstract-only analysis, and the evidence is based on a single longitudinal cohort. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to the lack of detailed statistical or clinical validation in the abstract.

Charge-driven antiviral responses enhance autoreactivity in severe COVID-19

Charge-driven antiviral responses enhance autoreactivity in severe COVID-19
作者： Renren Wen, Nathan Witman, Villalobos-Garcia D, Mei Yu, Archana Molangiri, Areeb Bajwa, Mary Beth Graham, Shawn Jobe, Weiguo Cui, Jieqing Zhu
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
该研究旨在调查在急性严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2感染期间出现的、对结构无关抗原具有广泛自身反应性和多反应性的抗病毒药物抗体的产生机制,因为这一现象不能完全用分子模拟来解释。
设计与对象
The study used BCR sequencing and recombinant antibody cloning from B cells of COVID-19 patients to analyze the acquisition of autoreactivity by antiviral antibodies.
核心方法
研究人员采用BCR测序和重组抗体克隆技术,检查来自严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2患者的抗病毒药物抗体互补决定区(CDRs)中正电荷残基的富集情况。
主要结果
种系回复分析表明,刺突蛋白 反应性(S2 结构域和 RBD)的增加与重链和轻链 CDR 中的净正电荷增加有关。此外,所有对带负电的 S2 亚基表现出反应性的带正电抗体也表现出增强的自身反应性。
解释与创新
研究结果表明,电荷驱动机制是 抗病毒药物 亲和力成熟的基础,将 抗病毒药物 免疫与自身反应性抗体的生成联系起来,而这一点以前未被认识到。
科研与公卫意义
These results provide insights into the mechanisms of autoreactivity in antiviral antibodies, which could inform the development of strategies to mitigate autoimmune responses in severe COVID-19 cases.
局限与证据强度
该研究仅基于抽象证据,这可能会限制分析的深度。然而,这些发现得到了 BCR 测序和重组抗体克隆的直接观察结果的支持,表明具有中等程度的置信度。

Charge-driven antiviral responses enhance autoreactivity in severe COVID-19

Authors: Renren Wen, Nathan Witman, Villalobos-Garcia D, Mei Yu, Archana Molangiri, Areeb Bajwa, Mary Beth Graham, Shawn Jobe, Weiguo Cui, Jieqing Zhu
Original abstract (English)
Abstract Viral infections are often accompanied by the emergence of antibodies that recognize both viral and self-antigens, a phenomenon largely attributed to molecular mimicry. However, this mechanism does not readily explain the emergence of antiviral antibodies with broad autoreactivity and polyreactivity toward structurally unrelated antigens during acute infection. Here, we demonstrate a charge-driven mechanism underlying the acquisition of autoreactivity by antiviral antibodies. Using BCR sequencing and recombinant antibody cloning from B cells of COVID-19 patients, we found that antiviral antibodies gained autoreactivity through enrichment of positively charged residues in complementarity-determining regions (CDRs). Germline reversion showed that increased spike protein reactivity (S2 domain and RBD) was associated with net positive charge gains in heavy- and light-chain CDRs. Critically, all the positively charged antibodies that gained reactivity to the negatively charged S2 subunit simultaneously increased autoreactivity. Docking and charge mutagenesis of interacting residues confirmed that positive charge is critical for both spike and autoantigen binding. At the population level, antibody repertoires against the more negatively charged Wuhan SARS-CoV-2 spike variant had significantly higher positive charge than those reacting to Omicron variants. Consistently, the charge of hemagglutinin variants and differing subunits drove similar repertoire differences in influenza. Together, these findings identify charge-driven antiviral affinity maturation as a previously unrecognized mechanism linking antiviral immunity to autoreactive antibody generation.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study aimed to investigate the mechanism behind the emergence of antiviral antibodies with broad autoreactivity and polyreactivity toward structurally unrelated antigens during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, as this phenomenon is not fully explained by molecular mimicry.
Design and population
The study used BCR sequencing and recombinant antibody cloning from B cells of COVID-19 patients to analyze the acquisition of autoreactivity by antiviral antibodies.
Core methods
The researchers employed BCR sequencing and recombinant antibody cloning techniques to examine the enrichment of positively charged residues in complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) of antiviral antibodies from SARS-CoV-2 patients.
Main results
Germline reversion analysis revealed that increased spike protein reactivity (S2 domain and RBD) was linked to net positive charge gains in heavy- and light-chain CDRs. Additionally, all positively charged antibodies that showed reactivity to the negatively charged S2 subunit also exhibited increased autoreactivity.
Interpretation and novelty
The findings suggest that a charge-driven mechanism underlies antiviral affinity maturation, linking antiviral immunity to autoreactive antibody generation, which was previously unrecognized.
Scientific and public-health significance
These results provide insights into the mechanisms of autoreactivity in antiviral antibodies, which could inform the development of strategies to mitigate autoimmune responses in severe COVID-19 cases.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is based on abstract-only evidence, which may limit the depth of analysis. However, the findings are supported by direct observations from BCR sequencing and recombinant antibody cloning, suggesting a moderate level of confidence.

补体增强 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的抗体中和。

Complement augments antibody neutralization of SARS-CoV-2 variants.
作者： M. Jungbauer-Groznica, Pierre Rosenbaum, Isabelle Staropoli, F. Guivel-Benhassine, Pierre‐Henri Commère, Tom Perisse, Lily Bruyère, Aura Fantin Rengifo, Alejandro De Cruz, Andréa Cottignies-Calamarte
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
补体系统是体液 免疫应答 的主要效应系统,但其与抗体配合抑制 宿主 中严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2) 传播的能力仍知之甚少。
设计与对象
在这里,我们结合了真实的病毒中和、抗体工程和流式病毒测定法的单个病毒颗粒分析,表明补体增强了 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的抗体中和。
核心方法
添加补体可使恢复期个体 (n = 14)、接种疫苗的个体 (n = 15) 和具有混合免疫个体 (n = 15) 的针对 D614G、BA.1、XBB.1.5 和 JN.1 变体的血清中和滴度增加高达 42 倍。
主要结果
D614G 和 BA.1 显示出高水平的中和作用,通过添加补体仅略有改善。相反,XBB.1.5 和 JN.1 的中和作用较弱,但被补体强烈增强。在 32 种 JN.1 非中和剂中,有 22 种在补体存在下恢复了可检测到的中和作用。
解释与创新
这种增强主要依赖于交叉反应性抗S2抗体,但也可以增强针对受体结合结构域和N端结构域的单克隆抗体。病毒抑制需要抗体 Fc 六聚化、C1q 募集和 C3 沉积,但它独立于 C9 形成的膜攻击复合物。
科研与公卫意义
Consistently, complement components were deposited at the surfaces of viral particles with no detectable virolysis. In sera from individuals with severe COVID-19, both complement-mediated neutralization and anti-S2 antibody levels were associated with improved survival.
局限与证据强度
总体而言,我们的数据表明补体增强了抗刺突抗体中和免疫逃避 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体的能力。

Complement augments antibody neutralization of SARS-CoV-2 variants.

Authors: M. Jungbauer-Groznica, Pierre Rosenbaum, Isabelle Staropoli, F. Guivel-Benhassine, Pierre‐Henri Commère, Tom Perisse, Lily Bruyère, Aura Fantin Rengifo, Alejandro De Cruz, Andréa Cottignies-Calamarte
Original abstract (English)
The complement system is a major effector system of the humoral immune response, but its capacity to cooperate with antibodies to inhibit the spread of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) in a host remains poorly characterized. Here, we combined authentic virus neutralization, antibody engineering, and single viral particle analysis by flow virometry to show that complement enhances antibody neutralization of SARS-CoV-2. Addition of complement increased neutralization titers of sera from convalescent individuals ( n = 14), vaccinated individuals ( n = 15), and individuals with hybrid immunity ( n = 15) against D614G, BA.1, XBB.1.5, and JN.1 variants by up to 42-fold. D614G and BA.1 displayed a high level of neutralization, which was only slightly improved by adding complement. Conversely, neutralization of XBB.1.5 and JN.1 was weak but strongly enhanced by complement. Among the 32 JN.1 nonneutralizers, 22 regained detectable neutralization in the presence of complement. The enhancement mainly relied on cross-reactive anti-S2 antibodies, but monoclonal antibodies targeting the receptor binding domain and N-terminal domain could also be augmented. Viral inhibition required antibody Fc hexamerization, C1q recruitment, and C3 deposition, but it was independent of the membrane attack complex formed by C9. Consistently, complement components were deposited at the surfaces of viral particles with no detectable virolysis. In sera from individuals with severe COVID-19, both complement-mediated neutralization and anti-S2 antibody levels were associated with improved survival. Overall, our data show that complement potentiates the ability of antispike antibodies to neutralize immune-evasive SARS-CoV-2 variants.

Escalation of CTX-M-producing extensively drug-resistant Shigella spp. in Kolkata, India, following the COVID-19 pandemic

Escalation of CTX-M-producing extensively drug-resistant Shigella spp. in Kolkata, India, following the COVID-19 pandemic
作者： Puja Bose, Gourab Halder, Pratanu Kayet, Goutam Chowdhury, Surajit Basak, Deboleena Roy, Daisuke Imamura, Shin-ichi Miyoshi, M. Morita, T. Ramamurthy
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
The study aimed to investigate the escalation of CTX-M-producing extensively drug-resistant Shigella spp. in Kolkata, India, following the COVID-19 pandemic, as Shigella is recognized by the World Health Organization as a high-priority pathogen due to its global prevalence, unique pathogenic mechanisms, and growing antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
设计与对象
The present study is based on prospective laboratory surveillance involving 323 Shigella isolates collected during 2021-2023, with pre-COVID-19 pandemic data included from a previously published study solely for historical comparison. Our prospective surveillance in Kolkata, India, reveals a worrisome escalation of third-generation cephalosporin resistance over the past decade, primarily associated with the spread of bla CTX-M-15 and the emergence of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) S.
核心方法
研究了抗生素抗性基因 (ARG) 的存在,并对代表性分离株进行全 基因组 测序 (WGS),以评估与全球分离株的系统发育相关性。携带 bla CTX-M-15 和 mphA 的质粒的检测,加上它们可转移性的证据,凸显了多药耐药性加速传播的潜力。
主要结果
虽然从 2013 年到 2019 年,只有 3% 的志贺氏菌分离株携带 bla CTX-M-15 基因,但到 2022 年到 2023 年,其 患病率 增加到 26%。这些分离株与英国报道的分离株有 48% 的克隆相似性和高度的系统发育相似性。杂交 基因组 组装揭示了一个含有 bla CTX-M-15 和 mphA ARG 的质粒。
解释与创新
志贺氏菌对第三代头孢菌素耐药性呈上升趋势,这主要是由产生广谱β-内酰胺酶的弗氏志贺氏菌的传播和XDR宋内志贺氏菌的出现所推动的,这凸显了加强国家AMR遏制战略和加强国际监测的迫切需要。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现为 治疗 指南、抗菌药物管理以及旨在遏制头孢菌素和阿奇霉素耐药志贺氏菌增长的国际遏制策略的设计提供了重要见解。
局限与证据强度
该研究基于实验室 监测,不包括详细的临床或流行病学数据,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。证据是温和的,因为它依赖于历史比较和基因组数据。

Escalation of CTX-M-producing extensively drug-resistant Shigella spp. in Kolkata, India, following the COVID-19 pandemic

Authors: Puja Bose, Gourab Halder, Pratanu Kayet, Goutam Chowdhury, Surajit Basak, Deboleena Roy, Daisuke Imamura, Shin-ichi Miyoshi, M. Morita, T. Ramamurthy
Original abstract (English)
is recognized by the World Health Organization as a high-priority pathogen due to its global prevalence, unique pathogenic mechanisms, and growing antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Nearly half of all Shigella strains worldwide are now multidrug-resistant (MDR), and the emergence of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) variants-resistant to ciprofloxacin, ceftriaxone, and azithromycin-has severely limited effective treatment options. The present study is based on prospective laboratory surveillance involving 323 Shigella isolates collected during 2021-2023, with pre-COVID-19 pandemic data included from a previously published study solely for historical comparison. The presence of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) was investigated, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on representative isolates to assess phylogenetic relatedness with global isolates. Approximately 10% of isolates exhibited resistance to third-generation cephalosporins. While only 3% of Shigella isolates carried the bla CTX-M-15 gene from 2013 to 2019, its prevalence increased to 26% by 2022-2023. Among 38 ceftriaxone-resistant S. sonnei isolates, 33 were also resistant to azithromycin, categorizing them as XDR. These isolates showed 48% clonal similarity and high phylogenetic resemblance to the isolates reported from England. Hybrid genome assembly revealed a plasmid harboring both the bla CTX-M-15 and mphA ARGs. Conjugation experiments and plasmid profiling confirmed the plasmid's transferability. We report a rising trend in third-generation cephalosporin resistance among Shigella spp., primarily driven by the spread of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing S. flexneri and the emergence of XDR S. These findings underscore the urgent need for strengthened national AMR containment strategies and enhanced international surveillance of cephalosporin-resistant Shigella to mitigate this growing public health threat.IMPORTANCE Shigella is a leading cause of diarrheal disease globally and has been prioritized by the World Health Organization due to its rapid acquisition of antimicrobial resistance. Our prospective surveillance in Kolkata, India, reveals a worrisome escalation of third-generation cephalosporin resistance over the past decade, primarily associated with the spread of bla CTX-M-15 and the emergence of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) S. The detection of plasmids carrying both bla CTX-M-15 and mphA , coupled with evidence of their transferability, highlights the potential for accelerated dissemination of multidrug resistance. When compared with a global data set of international genomes, the Kolkata XDR isolates were found to cluster closely with isolates reported from England. By linking local surveillance with global genomic context, our findings provide critical insights for treatment guidelines, antimicrobial stewardship, and the design of international containment strategies aimed at curbing the rise of cephalosporin- and azithromycin-resistant Shigella .
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study aimed to investigate the escalation of CTX-M-producing extensively drug-resistant Shigella spp. in Kolkata, India, following the COVID-19 pandemic, as Shigella is recognized by the World Health Organization as a high-priority pathogen due to its global prevalence, unique pathogenic mechanisms, and growing antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
Design and population
The present study is based on prospective laboratory surveillance involving 323 Shigella isolates collected during 2021-2023, with pre-COVID-19 pandemic data included from a previously published study solely for historical comparison. Our prospective surveillance in Kolkata, India, reveals a worrisome escalation of third-generation cephalosporin resistance over the past decade, primarily associated with the spread of bla CTX-M-15 and the emergence of extensively drug-resistant (XDR) S.
Core methods
The presence of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) was investigated, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on representative isolates to assess phylogenetic relatedness with global isolates. The detection of plasmids carrying both bla CTX-M-15 and mphA, coupled with evidence of their transferability, highlights the potential for accelerated dissemination of multidrug resistance.
Main results
While only 3% of Shigella isolates carried the bla CTX-M-15 gene from 2013 to 2019, its prevalence increased to 26% by 2022-2023. These isolates showed 48% clonal similarity and high phylogenetic resemblance to the isolates reported from England. Hybrid genome assembly revealed a plasmid harboring both the bla CTX-M-15 and mphA ARGs.
Interpretation and novelty
The rising trend in third-generation cephalosporin resistance among Shigella spp., primarily driven by the spread of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing S. flexneri and the emergence of XDR S. sonnei, highlights the urgent need for strengthened national AMR containment strategies and enhanced international surveillance.
Scientific and public-health significance
These findings provide critical insights for treatment guidelines, antimicrobial stewardship, and the design of international containment strategies aimed at curbing the rise of cephalosporin- and azithromycin-resistant Shigella.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is based on laboratory surveillance and does not include detailed clinical or epidemiological data, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. The evidence is moderate, as it relies on historical comparisons and genomic data.

ADDRESS-LC:一项 2 期、三盲、随机、安慰剂对照试验的研究方案,旨在评估 Bezisterim (NE3107) 对成人 长新冠 的疗效和安全性。

ADDRESS-LC: study protocol for a phase 2, triple-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bezisterim (NE3107) in adults with long COVID.
作者： P. Markham, M. Peluso, Sherry Hsiang-Yi Chou, L. McCorkell, S. O'Quinn, Christopher Lewis Reading, Clarence N Ahlem, Chantal M Petit, Jiayan Yan, Joseph M. Palumbo
摘要中文翻译简介 长新冠 是一种使人衰弱的疾病,包括认知障碍(“脑雾”)和睡眠障碍等长期神经系统症状。症状可能与病毒 刺突蛋白 的持续存在、其他病毒的激活、延长的巨噬细胞炎症记忆或通过 Toll 样受体 (TLR) 信号传导刺激促炎细胞因子的持久病毒 刺突蛋白 引起的持续神经炎症有关。Bezisterim (NE3107) 是一种口服、血脑屏障可渗透、抗炎、胰岛素增敏的脱氢表雄酮衍生物,可抑制 TLR 驱动的神经炎症,目前正在开发用于治疗 TLR 驱动的炎症导致认知能力下降的神经退行性疾病。方法和分析 ADDRESS-LC (NCT06847191) 是一项 2 期、三盲、安慰剂对照、随机概念验证研究,旨在评估 Bezisterim 对成人 长新冠 的疗效和安全性。这项多中心研究将招募 208 名在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后至少 3 个月内出现疲劳和神经认知障碍症状的成年人(年龄 18-69 岁)。符合所有资格标准的个人将以 1:1 的比例随机接受 20 mg 贝齐斯特林或安慰剂,每天两次,持续 12 周。认知、疲劳、睡眠、劳累后不适、生活质量和繁重症状将通过多项评估进行评估,包括定制的 Cogstate 认知电池、患者报告结果测量信息系统 (PROMIS) 认知功能简表 (SF)-8a、PROMIS 疲劳 SF-13a 和患者对严重程度的总体印象等。伦理与传播 该方案在研究开始前已获得机构审查委员会的批准。该研究正在美国多个临床研究中心进行。当前参与研究地点的列表可通过 ClinicalTrials.gov 注册记录 (NCT06847191) 公开获取。该研究方案已获得中央机构审查委员会的批准(Advarra #Pro00081088),参与中心根据适用法规和良好临床实践指南获得了研究实施和数据访问所需的必要批准和协议。申办者、监管机构和伦理委员会的授权代表可以在参与者知情同意的情况下出于监测、审计和监管目的访问研究相关记录。该研究将通过学术出版物和会议演讲来传播结果。试用注册号NCT06847191。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
这项研究需要解决 长新冠 的衰弱影响,特别是长期的神经系统症状,如认知障碍和睡眠障碍。目的是评估贝齐斯特林治疗这些症状的有效性和安全性。
设计与对象
该研究是一项 2 期、三盲、随机、安慰剂对照试验,旨在评估贝齐斯特林治疗 长新冠 成人的效果。它将招募 208 名年龄在 18-69 岁之间的成年人,他们在 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染后至少 3 个月内出现疲劳和神经认知障碍症状。
核心方法
该研究将使用多项评估来评估认知、疲劳、睡眠、劳累后不适、生活质量和繁重症状,包括 Cogstate 认知电池、PROMIS 认知功能简表 (SF)-8a、PROMIS 疲劳 SF-13a 和患者对严重程度的总体印象。参与者将以 1:1 的比例随机接受 20 mg 贝齐斯特林或安慰剂,每天两次,持续 12 周。
主要结果
该研究将通过指定的评估直接观察认知、疲劳、睡眠、劳累后不适、生活质量和负担症状的变化。
解释与创新
作者解释说,bezisterim 可能会解决与 长新冠 相关的神经炎症,提供一种通过 TLR 驱动的炎症抑制来控制其症状的新方法。
科研与公卫意义
这些发现可以为 长新冠 未来的 治疗 策略提供信息,特别是在针对神经炎症和改善受影响个体的认知和身体症状方面。
局限与证据强度
该研究是一项概念验证试验,样本量有限,这可能会限制结果的普遍性。证据是温和的,因为它是基于协议而不是实际结果。

ADDRESS-LC: study protocol for a phase 2, triple-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bezisterim (NE3107) in adults with long COVID.

Authors: P. Markham, M. Peluso, Sherry Hsiang-Yi Chou, L. McCorkell, S. O'Quinn, Christopher Lewis Reading, Clarence N Ahlem, Chantal M Petit, Jiayan Yan, Joseph M. Palumbo
Original abstract (English)
Introduction Long COVID is a debilitating condition consisting of prolonged neurological symptoms such as cognitive impairment ('brain fog') and sleep disturbance. Symptoms may be associated with ongoing neuroinflammation from the persistence of a viral reservoir, activation of other viruses, protracted macrophagic inflammatory memory or enduring viral Spike protein that stimulates proinflammatory cytokines via toll-like receptor (TLR) signalling. Bezisterim (NE3107) is an oral, blood-brain barrier-permeable, anti-inflammatory, insulin-sensitising dehydroepiandrosterone derivative that inhibits TLR-driven neuroinflammation and is being developed for neurodegenerative diseases in which TLR-driven inflammation contributes to cognitive decline. Methods and analysis ADDRESS-LC (NCT06847191) is a phase 2, triple-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised proof-of-concept study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bezisterim in adults with long COVID. This multicentre study will recruit 208 adults (aged 18-69 years) with symptoms of fatigue and neurocognitive impairment for at least 3 months following an index SARS-CoV-2 infection. Individuals who meet all eligibility criteria will be randomised 1:1 to receive bezisterim 20 mg or placebo two times per day for 12 weeks. Cognition, fatigue, sleep, post-exertional malaise, quality of life and burdensome symptoms will be evaluated via several assessments, including a bespoke Cogstate Cognition Battery, Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) Cognitive Function Short Form (SF)-8a, PROMIS Fatigue SF-13a and Patient's Global Impression of Severity, among others. Ethics and dissemination The protocol has been approved by an institutional review board prior to study initiation. The study is being conducted at multiple clinical research sites across the USA. A current list of participating study sites is publicly available through the ClinicalTrials.gov registration record (NCT06847191). The study protocol has received central institutional review board approval (Advarra #Pro00081088), and participating sites obtained the necessary approvals and agreements required for study conduct and data access in accordance with applicable regulations and Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Authorised representatives of the sponsor, regulatory authorities and ethics committees may access study-related records for monitoring, auditing and regulatory purposes consistent with participant informed consent. The study will disseminate results through academic publication and conference presentations. Trial registration number NCT06847191.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study was needed to address the debilitating effects of long COVID, particularly prolonged neurological symptoms such as cognitive impairment and sleep disturbance. The objective is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of bezisterim in managing these symptoms.
Design and population
The study is a phase 2, triple-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial designed to assess bezisterim in adults with long COVID. It will recruit 208 adults aged 18-69 years who have experienced symptoms of fatigue and neurocognitive impairment for at least 3 months following an index SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Core methods
The study will evaluate cognition, fatigue, sleep, post-exertional malaise, quality of life and burdensome symptoms using several assessments, including the Cogstate Cognition Battery, PROMIS Cognitive Function Short Form (SF)-8a, PROMIS Fatigue SF-13a and Patient's Global Impression of Severity. Participants will be randomised 1:1 to receive bezisterim 20 mg or placebo twice daily for 12 weeks.
Main results
The study will directly observe changes in cognition, fatigue, sleep, post-exertional malaise, quality of life and burdensome symptoms through the specified assessments.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpret that bezisterim may address neuroinflammation associated with long COVID, offering a novel approach to managing its symptoms through TLR-driven inflammation inhibition.
Scientific and public-health significance
The findings could inform future treatment strategies for long COVID, particularly in targeting neuroinflammation and improving cognitive and physical symptoms in affected individuals.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is a proof-of-concept trial with a limited sample size, which may restrict the generalisability of the results. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a protocol and not yet on actual outcomes.

原子分辨率下 3 类和 4 类抗体的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 尖峰中和的局部刚性化和变构调节机制:结合、动力学和变构的综合计算研究

Localized Rigidification and Allosteric Modulation Mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Neutralization by Class 3 and Class 4 Antibodies at Atomic Resolution: An Integrated Computational Study of Binding, Dynamics, and Allostery
作者： Mohammed Alshahrani, Will Gatlin, Max Ludwick, Lucas Turano, Brandon Foley, Gennady M. Verkhivker
摘要中文翻译摘要 进化 的无情 进化 和高度抗体规避变体的出现强调需要破译控制抗体中和广度和弹性的分子原理。在本研究中,我们采用结合结构分析、构象动力学、突变扫描、结合能量学和变构网络建模的集成计算框架来剖析针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 受体结合域 (RBD) 的 3 类和 4 类抗体的机制特征。通过对包括单个抗体(COV2-3835、COV2-3891、COV2-3906)和协同双抗体对在内的抗体-RBD复合物进行全面分析,我们发现了区分这两种抗体类别的基本机制二分法,并解释了它们中和效力、广度和病毒逃逸能力的差异模式。我们的分析表明,3 类抗体通过严格限制在结合界面的机械扰动实现中和。相比之下,4 类抗体采用长程变构不稳定机制,锚定在结构刚性的疏水核心上,并通过 β-折叠核心建立机械管道,传递构象变化。突变扫描和严格的能量分析揭示了根本不同的脆弱性景观:4类表位由不可变的疏水核心定义,该核心对突变极其敏感,但在sarbecoviruses中受到进化限制,解释了它们的超广泛结合和有限的逃逸潜力。3 类表位呈现出具有保守锚定的塑料外围,并且外围区域的敏感性可变,从而创建多个逃逸途径。这些预测与实验深度突变扫描数据非常吻合,验证了我们的计算方法并建立了预测免疫逃逸的定量框架。变构网络分析将 β-片层核心确定为 4 类抗体的关键通讯管道,其中特定残基充当将疏水核心连接到 RBM 环的重要枢纽。这些位置的高通讯中心性与极端扰动敏感性的融合使它们成为最关键的变构热点,对功能至关重要并能抵抗 突变。所提出的多管齐下的计算框架为理解抗体中和机制和预测不同病毒靶标的免疫逃逸提供了一种通用的方法,对平衡效力、广度和弹性的下一代抗体疗法的合理设计具有影响。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 的无情 进化 和高度抗体规避变体的出现强调需要破译控制抗体中和广度和弹性的分子原理。
设计与对象
在本研究中,我们采用结合结构分析、构象动力学、突变扫描、结合能量学和变构网络建模的集成计算框架来剖析针对 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 刺突蛋白 受体结合域 (RBD) 的 3 类和 4 类抗体的机制特征。
核心方法
通过对包括单个抗体(COV2-3835、COV2-3891、COV2-3906)和协同双抗体对在内的抗体-RBD复合物进行全面分析,我们发现了区分这两种抗体类别的基本机制二分法,并解释了它们中和效力、广度和病毒逃逸能力的差异模式。
主要结果
我们的分析表明,3 类抗体通过严格限制在结合界面的机械扰动实现中和,而 4 类抗体则采用长程变构去稳定机制,锚定到结构刚性的疏水核心,并通过 β-片层核心建立机械导管,传递构象变化。
解释与创新
突变扫描和严格的能量分析揭示了根本不同的脆弱性景观:4类表位由不可变的疏水核心定义,该核心对突变极其敏感,但在所有sarbecoviruses中都受到进化限制,解释了它们的超宽结合和有限的逃逸潜力,而3类表位则表现出具有保守锚点的塑料外围和外围区域的可变敏感性,从而创造了多种逃逸途径。
科研与公卫意义
所提出的多管齐下的计算框架为理解抗体中和机制和预测不同病毒靶标的免疫逃逸提供了一种通用的方法,对平衡效力、广度和弹性的下一代抗体疗法的合理设计具有影响。
局限与证据强度
所提供的证据并未报告该研究的具体局限性。然而,计算预测和实验深度突变扫描数据之间的良好一致性验证了该方法,并建立了预测免疫逃逸的定量框架,表明证据强度很高。

Localized Rigidification and Allosteric Modulation Mechanisms of SARS-CoV-2 Spike Neutralization by Class 3 and Class 4 Antibodies at Atomic Resolution: An Integrated Computational Study of Binding, Dynamics, and Allostery

Authors: Mohammed Alshahrani, Will Gatlin, Max Ludwick, Lucas Turano, Brandon Foley, Gennady M. Verkhivker
Original abstract (English)
Abstract The relentless evolution of SARS-CoV-2 and the emergence of highly antibody-evasive variants underscore the need to decipher the molecular principles that govern antibody neutralization breadth and resilience. In this study, we employ an integrated computational framework combining structural analysis, conformational dynamics, mutational scanning, binding energetics, and allosteric network modeling to dissect the mechanistic signatures of class 3 and class 4 antibodies targeting the receptor-binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein. Through comprehensive analysis of antibody-RBD complexes including individual antibodies (COV2-3835, COV2-3891, COV2-3906) and synergistic dual-antibody pairs we uncover a fundamental mechanistic dichotomy that distinguishes these two antibody classes and explains their differential patterns of neutralization potency, breadth, and resilience to viral escape. Our analysis reveals that class 3 antibodies achieve neutralization with mechanical perturbation strictly confined to the binding interface. In contrast, class 4 antibodies employ a long-range allosteric destabilization mechanism, anchoring to a structurally rigid hydrophobic core and establishing a mechanical conduit through the β-sheet core that transmits conformational changes. Mutational scanning and rigorous energetic analysis reveal fundamentally different vulnerability landscapes: class 4 epitopes are defined by an immutable hydrophobic core that is exquisitely sensitive to mutation yet evolutionarily constrained across sarbecoviruses, explaining their ultra-broad binding and limited escape potential. Class 3 epitopes exhibit a plastic periphery with a conserved anchor and variable sensitivity in peripheral regions, creating multiple escape pathways. These predictions show excellent agreement with experimental deep mutational scanning data, validating our computational approach and establishing a quantitative framework for predicting immune escape. Allosteric network analysis identifies the β-sheet core as the critical communication conduit for class 4 antibodies, with specific residues serving as essential hubs that connect the hydrophobic core to the RBM loop. The convergence of high communication centrality with extreme perturbation sensitivity at these positions establishes them as the most critical allosteric hotspots, essential for function and resistant to mutation. The proposed multi-pronged computational framework provides a generalizable approach for understanding antibody neutralization mechanisms and predicting immune escape across diverse viral targets, with implications for the rational design of next-generation antibody therapeutics that balance potency, breadth, and resilience.

Scientific and public-health significance
The proposed multi-pronged computational framework provides a generalizable approach for understanding antibody neutralization mechanisms and predicting immune escape across diverse viral targets, with implications for the rational design of next-generation antibody therapeutics that balance potency, breadth, and resilience.

However, the excellent agreement between computational predictions and experimental deep mutational scanning data validates the approach and establishes a quantitative framework for predicting immune escape, suggesting high evidence strength.

Most COVID-19 vaccine adverse events detected within 48 hours in Ethiopia: implications for cohort event monitoring efficiency in resource-limited settings

Most COVID-19 vaccine adverse events detected within 48 hours in Ethiopia: implications for cohort event monitoring efficiency in resource-limited settings
作者： Tigist Dires Gebreyesus, Teshita Shute, Asnakech Alemu, A. Berha, Mehiret Maru, Habtamu Gashaw, M. Kifle, Julie Doherty, Albert Figueras
摘要中文翻译
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
The study addressed the operational feasibility of the WHO-recommended 30-day cohort event monitoring (CEM) for COVID-19 vaccine safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where resource constraints challenge extended follow-up periods.
设计与对象
A prospective active surveillance study was conducted in Ethiopia from August 2021 to June 2022, enrolling 10,948 adults who received the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine, with follow-up via immediate observation and telephone contacts on days 2, 4, 7, 14, 21, and 30.
核心方法
通过立即观察和按预定时间间隔进行结构化电话随访,监测参与者的免疫接种后不良事件 (AEFI),无需额外的实验室或诊断程序即可捕获所有报告的症状。
主要结果
在 10,948 名参与者中,4,236 名(38.7%;95% CI:37.8–39.6%)报告至少有 1 次 AEFI,总共记录了 6,174 起事件;88.2% 的事件在 48 小时内检测到(1.8% 立即检测到,86.4% 在第 2 天检测到),11.8% 发生在第 4 天到第 30 天之间。
解释与创新
The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that most COVID-19 vaccine adverse events in Ethiopia occur within 48 hours, suggesting that extended full-cohort CEM may yield diminishing returns in LMIC settings, and proposed a hybrid surveillance model to optimize resource use.
科研与公卫意义
结果支持从长期扩展监测转向结合短期主动 监测、增强被动报告和哨兵网络的混合方法,为类似情况下的紧急 疫苗 安全 疫苗 提供更可持续的药物警戒框架。
局限与证据强度
该研究受到单一国家、单一 疫苗 设计的限制,并且依赖于未经实验室确认的自我报告症状,这可能会低估或错误分类事件;鉴于不存在严重的 AEFI 和操作重点,证据强度中等。

Most COVID-19 vaccine adverse events detected within 48 hours in Ethiopia: implications for cohort event monitoring efficiency in resource-limited settings

Authors: Tigist Dires Gebreyesus, Teshita Shute, Asnakech Alemu, A. Berha, Mehiret Maru, Habtamu Gashaw, M. Kifle, Julie Doherty, Albert Figueras
Original abstract (English)
Background The World Health Organization recommends cohort event monitoring with a 30-day follow-up period for vaccine safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). However, in resource-limited settings, operational and logistical constraints necessitate evaluation of the efficiency and feasibility of this follow-up duration. Methods We conducted an analysis of a prospective active surveillance study of 10,948 adults who received the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine in Ethiopia (August 2021-June 2022), using immediate observation and telephone follow-up on days 2, 4, 7, 14, 21, and 30. Results Among 10,948 participants, 4,236 (38.7%; 95% CI: 37.8-39.6%) reported at least one adverse event following immunisation (AEFI), with 6,174 total events recorded. Of all events, 88.2% were detected within 48 h (1.8% immediate, 86.4% at day 2), while 11.8% were identified during subsequent follow-up between days 4 and 30. Seven reactogenic symptoms comprised 93.8% of AEFIs. No serious AEFIs or adverse events of special interest were identified. Over nine months, 138 healthcare professionals captured predominantly mild, expected reactions through extended surveillance. Conclusions Most COVID-19 vaccine adverse events in Ethiopia occurred within 48 h of vaccination, empirically suggesting that extended full-cohort CEM could yield diminishing informational returns in low- and middle-income country settings. A hybrid surveillance approach combining intensive short-term active surveillance during the first 48 h, enhanced passive reporting, and sentinel hospital networks with adequate diagnostic capacity could offer a more sustainable and operationally realistic framework. These findings are offered as an evidence-based reference for national regulatory authorities planning or conducting emergency vaccine safety surveillance in comparable contexts, supporting a transition from product-centred extended monitoring towards patient-centred, resource-adapted pharmacovigilance. Clinical trial number Not applicable.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study addressed the operational feasibility of the WHO-recommended 30-day cohort event monitoring (CEM) for COVID-19 vaccine safety surveillance in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where resource constraints challenge extended follow-up periods.
Design and population
A prospective active surveillance study was conducted in Ethiopia from August 2021 to June 2022, enrolling 10,948 adults who received the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine, with follow-up via immediate observation and telephone contacts on days 2, 4, 7, 14, 21, and 30.
Core methods
Participants were monitored for adverse events following immunization (AEFI) through immediate observation and structured telephone follow-up at predefined intervals, capturing all reported symptoms without additional laboratory or diagnostic procedures.
Main results
Among 10,948 participants, 4,236 (38.7%; 95% CI: 37.8–39.6%) reported at least one AEFI, with 6,174 total events recorded; 88.2% of events were detected within 48 hours (1.8% immediate, 86.4% at day 2), and 11.8% occurred between days 4 and 30.
Interpretation and novelty
The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that most COVID-19 vaccine adverse events in Ethiopia occur within 48 hours, suggesting that extended full-cohort CEM may yield diminishing returns in LMIC settings, and proposed a hybrid surveillance model to optimize resource use.
Scientific and public-health significance
The results support a shift from prolonged extended monitoring to a hybrid approach combining short-term active surveillance, enhanced passive reporting, and sentinel networks, offering a more sustainable pharmacovigilance framework for emergency vaccine safety surveillance in comparable contexts.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study was limited by its single-country, single-vaccine design and reliance on self-reported symptoms without laboratory confirmation, which may underestimate or misclassify events; the evidence strength is moderate given the absence of serious AEFIs and the operational focus.

严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体 PQ.16.1.1 和 RK.1 的抗体逃避和受体结合

Antibody evasion and receptor binding of SARS-CoV-2 variants PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1
作者： Peizhuo He, Yunwen Song, Chipeng Guo, Lingling Yu, Yuanling Yu, Fanchong Jian, Fei Shao, Yunlong Cao
摘要中文翻译严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 变体 NB.1.8.1 最近在全球范围内的扩张推动了 PQ.16.1.1 和 RK.1 亚​​系的出现,它们在其受体结合域中独立获得了 D420N 突变,目前在亚太地区占据主导地位。利用表面等离振子共振和假病毒测定的评估表明,与亲代菌株相比,这些亚系表现出显着降低的人类 ACE2 受体结合。然而,这种功能成本被逃避体液免疫的显着能力所抵消,特别是表现出对 1 类中和单克隆抗体和来自 Wuu-Hu-1 引发个体的恢复期血浆的深刻抵抗力。这种收敛的 进化 体现了经典的病毒权衡,牺牲受体结合效率来逃避群体水平的免疫压力。因此,这些发现表明这些变体将很快在全球传播,并强调持续进行 监测 监测 D420N 携带谱系的迫切需要。
查看研究七要素
问题与背景
该研究旨在调查严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体PQ.16.1.1和RK.1的出现和特征,这些变体在其受体结合域中获得了D420N 突变,目前在亚太地区占主导地位。
设计与对象
该研究通过表面等离子共振和假病毒检测评估了这些变体的功能特性,重点关注它们与人类 ACE2 受体的相互作用和免疫逃避能力。
核心方法
研究人员使用表面等离振子共振和假病毒测定来评估受体结合和中和抗性,将变异体与其亲本毒株和来自武汉-Hu-1引发的个体的恢复期血浆进行比较。
主要结果
与亲代菌株相比,PQ.16.1.1 和 RK.1 亚​​谱系显示出人类 ACE2 受体结合显着降低,同时表现出对 1 类中和单克隆抗体和恢复期血浆的强烈抵抗力。
解释与创新
这些发现强调了一种经典的病毒权衡,即这些变体牺牲受体结合效率来逃避免疫压力,这表明它们具有全球传播的潜力。
科研与公卫意义
这些结果强调了正在进行的 监测 对于 D420N 携带谱系的重要性,并为更新诊断和治疗策略的开发提供了信息。
局限与证据强度
该研究仅限于体外测定,并未考虑体内动力学,但鉴于对变体的直接功能评估,证据是强有力的。

Antibody evasion and receptor binding of SARS-CoV-2 variants PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1

Authors: Peizhuo He, Yunwen Song, Chipeng Guo, Lingling Yu, Yuanling Yu, Fanchong Jian, Fei Shao, Yunlong Cao
Original abstract (English)
The recent global expansion of the SARS-CoV-2 variant NB.1.8.1 has driven the emergence of sublineages PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1, which independently acquired the D420N mutation in their receptor-binding domains and and now dominate the Asia-Pacific region. Evaluations utilizing surface plasmon resonance and pseudovirus assays demonstrate that these sublineages exhibit significantly reduced human ACE2 receptor engagement compared to their parental strain. However, this functional cost is offset by a marked ability to evade humoral immunity, specifically demonstrating profound resistance to Class 1 neutralizing monoclonal antibodies and convalescent plasma from Wuhan-Hu-1-primed individuals. This convergent evolution exemplifies a classical viral trade-off, sacrificing receptor binding efficiency to escape population-level immune pressure. Consequently, these findings suggest these variants will soon spread globally and emphasize the critical need for ongoing surveillance to monitor D420N-carrying lineages.
View research seven-element analysis
Question and background
The study aimed to investigate the emergence and characteristics of SARS-CoV-2 variants PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1, which have acquired the D420N mutation in their receptor-binding domains and are now dominant in the Asia-Pacific region.
Design and population
The study evaluated the functional properties of these variants through surface plasmon resonance and pseudovirus assays, focusing on their interaction with the human ACE2 receptor and immune evasion capabilities.
Core methods
The researchers used surface plasmon resonance and pseudovirus assays to assess receptor binding and neutralization resistance, comparing the variants to their parental strain and convalescent plasma from Wuhan-Hu-1-primed individuals.
Main results
The sublineages PQ.16.1.1 and RK.1 showed significantly reduced human ACE2 receptor engagement compared to their parental strain, while demonstrating profound resistance to Class 1 neutralizing monoclonal antibodies and convalescent plasma.
Interpretation and novelty
The findings highlight a classical viral trade-off, where these variants sacrifice receptor binding efficiency to evade immune pressure, suggesting their potential for global spread.
Scientific and public-health significance
These results underscore the importance of ongoing surveillance for D420N-carrying lineages and inform the development of updated diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
Limitations and evidence strength
The study is limited to in vitro assays and does not account for in vivo dynamics, but the evidence is strong given the direct functional evaluations of the variants.

SARS-CoV-2 and neutralizing antibody dynamics at a remote village in Kenya before widespread COVID-19 vaccine rollout

SARS-CoV-2 and neutralizing antibody dynamics at a remote village in Kenya before widespread COVID-19 vaccine rollout
作者： Esther Omuseni, Josphat Nyataya, Peter Sifuna, George Awinda, Allan Lemtudo, Clement Masakhwe, Beth Mutai, Geoffrey M. Maina, Simon K Kariuki, John Waitumbi
摘要中文翻译
查看综述五要素
范围与问题
该研究重点关注 疫苗 覆盖范围有限的肯尼亚农村人口中的 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染率和中和抗体动态,特别评估感染 患病率 和人群水平中和抗体的增加。
证据基础与方法
这是一项在 KEMRI/WRAIR-非洲健康人口统计 监测 系统中进行的纵向研究,涉及 160,000 人。2021 年 4 月至 2022 年 3 月期间,在 Alpha、Delta 和 Omicron 浪潮期间,开展了六项横断面调查,每次针对 234 名参与者,间隔两个月。收集鼻咽样本和血清用于 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 检测和使用替代病毒中和测试的中和抗体测量。
共识与结论
在 Omicron 期间,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染率从 3% 增加到 24%,然后下降到零,最后上升到 10%。中和抗体总体从 18% 增加到 86%,几何平均值从 0.42 U/mL 增加到 9.4 U/mL。女性的 Nab 含量高于男性,并且 Nab 的数量随着年龄的增长而增加。
争议与缺口
由于非药物干预措施和个体水平变量等未测量因素,该研究无法自信地推断中和抗体与 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 感染减少之间的因果关系。
科研与实践启示
研究结果强调了在农村、低 疫苗 覆盖率环境中研究 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 传播 和免疫力的重要性,以了解此类人群中的感染动态和 免疫应答。

SARS-CoV-2 and neutralizing antibody dynamics at a remote village in Kenya before widespread COVID-19 vaccine rollout

Authors: Esther Omuseni, Josphat Nyataya, Peter Sifuna, George Awinda, Allan Lemtudo, Clement Masakhwe, Beth Mutai, Geoffrey M. Maina, Simon K Kariuki, John Waitumbi
Original abstract (English)
Given limited data on SARS‐CoV‐2 transmission and immunity in rural, low‐vaccine‐coverage settings, we evaluated infection rates and population‐level neutralizing antibody increase in a rural community in western Kenya. The study was conducted at the KEMRI/WRAIR-Africa Health Demographic Surveillance System that has a population of 160,000. Clusters of households that had representative demographics were identified and individuals invited to participate in six cross-sectional surveys that targeted 234 participants at each survey, two months apart, conducted between April 2021 and March 2022, during which time, the Alpha, Delta and Omicron waves dominated. At each survey, participants provided naso-pharyngeal samples for SARS-CoV-2 detection and serum for measuring neutralizing antibodies (NAbs) using surrogate virus neutralizing test which assessed inhibition of RBD–ACE2 binding. 69% (917/1329) of the participants were females. By RT-qPCR, SARS-CoV-2 increased from 3% (7/224) at survey one (April 2021) to 24% (55/229) by survey two (June 2021), and thereafter decreased to zero, only to rise to 10% (23/234) during the January 2022 Omicron wave. NAbs increased from 18% (40/224) at survey one to 86% (202/234) by end of the study. The quantity of NAbs rose from geometric mean of 0.42 U/mL at survey one to 9.4 U/mL by survey six. Females had higher NAbs (3.73U/mL, 95% CI), compared to 1.98 U/mL, 95% CI (p = 0.0146) for males. NAbs quantities increased with age: 2.1 U/mL for 60 years. The increase in population-level NAbs is consistent with widespread exposure to the virus during the study period. As caveat, causality of NAbs for the decline in SARS‐CoV‐2 infections cannot be inferred with confidence, because other factors such as the use of non‐pharmaceutical interventions and other individual-level variables were not measured.
View review five-element analysis
Scope and question
The study focused on SARS-CoV-2 infection rates and neutralizing antibody dynamics in a rural Kenyan population with limited vaccine coverage, specifically evaluating infection prevalence and population-level neutralizing antibody increases.
Evidence base and method
This was a longitudinal study conducted at the KEMRI/WRAIR-Africa Health Demographic Surveillance System with 160,000 people. Six cross-sectional surveys targeted 234 participants each, two months apart, between April 2021 and March 2022, during Alpha, Delta, and Omicron waves. Naso-pharyngeal samples and serum were collected for SARS-CoV-2 detection and neutralizing antibody measurement using surrogate virus neutralizing tests.
Consensus and conclusions
SARS-CoV-2 infection rates increased from 3% to 24% then decreased to zero before rising to 10% during Omicron. Neutralizing antibodies increased from 18% to 86% overall, with geometric mean rising from 0.42 U/mL to 9.4 U/mL. Females had higher NAbs than males, and NAbs quantities increased with age.
Controversies and gaps
The study could not confidently infer causality between neutralizing antibodies and reduced SARS-CoV-2 infections due to unmeasured factors like non-pharmaceutical interventions and individual-level variables.
Research and practice implications
The findings highlight the importance of studying SARS-CoV-2 transmission and immunity in rural, low-vaccine-coverage settings to understand infection dynamics and immune responses in such populations.

Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV Vaccinations for Immunocompromised Children and Household Contacts.

Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV Vaccinations for Immunocompromised Children and Household Contacts.
作者： Carol M. Kao, Hannah Bahakel, T. Heald-Sargent, Timothy D. Minniear, Victoria A. Statler, Sanya J. Thomas, Kathryn E. Weakley, Qing Cao, Monica I. Ardura, Lara A. Danziger-Isakov
摘要中文翻译
查看综述五要素
范围与问题
The review focuses on immunocompromised pediatric patients, including hematopoietic cell and solid organ transplant recipients, those undergoing chemotherapy for malignancy, and those receiving biologic response modifiers for autoimmune or inflammatory conditions, who are at risk for severe disease from vaccine-preventable respiratory viral infections such as influenza, SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The central question is to review available data supporting current guidelines regarding vaccine dosing, scheduling, and formulations to prevent these infections in immunocompromised children.
证据基础与方法
该综述是对现有数据的叙述性综合,因为没有报告具体的数据库、检索日期、资格标准或研究计数。作者的目的是回顾现有指南并强调知识差距,但没有描述系统搜索或荟萃分析。
共识与结论
由于免疫系统不成熟、免疫记忆缺失和环境暴露增加等因素,免疫功能低下的儿童面临更高的住院率、重症监护率和 死亡率 率。目前的免疫建议主要是根据健康儿童和/或免疫功能低下成人的研究推断的,因为缺乏有关该人群免疫反应和 疫苗 功效的主要数据。
争议与缺口
关于免疫反应和 疫苗 疗效(特别是在免疫功能低下儿童中)的主要数据很少。此外,免疫功能低下儿童及其家庭接触者中 疫苗 犹豫的趋势、持续的社区 传播 以及次优的 疫苗接种 率也加剧了风险。在改善呼吸道病毒 疫苗 免疫原性和优化保护方面存在关键知识差距。
科研与实践启示
随着患有免疫功能低下的儿童数量的增加,初级保健从业者和专科医生必须确保为这些患者及其家庭和社区接触者提供适当的免疫接种。未来的研究应集中于提高 疫苗 的免疫原性和对这一弱势群体的保护。

Influenza, COVID-19, and RSV Vaccinations for Immunocompromised Children and Household Contacts.

Authors: Carol M. Kao, Hannah Bahakel, T. Heald-Sargent, Timothy D. Minniear, Victoria A. Statler, Sanya J. Thomas, Kathryn E. Weakley, Qing Cao, Monica I. Ardura, Lara A. Danziger-Isakov
Original abstract (English)
Immunocompromised pediatric patients, including hematopoietic cell and solid organ transplant recipients, those undergoing chemotherapy for malignancy, and those receiving biologic response modifiers for autoimmune or inflammatory conditions, are at risk for severe disease from vaccine-preventable respiratory viral infections such as influenza, SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). These children face higher rates of hospitalization, intensive care admissions, and mortality, reflecting contributions from an immature immune system, absence of immunologic memory, and/or increased environmental exposures. Immunization recommendations for immunocompromised children are largely extrapolated from studies conducted among healthy children and/or immunocompromised adults due to a paucity of primary data on immunological responses and vaccine efficacy in immunocompromised children. Trends in vaccine hesitancy in the general population, ongoing transmission of respiratory viral infections in the community, and suboptimal vaccination rates among immunocompromised children and their household contacts further compound the risk for this vulnerable population. As the number of children with immunocompromising conditions expands, it is imperative that primary care practitioners and subspecialists who care for immunocompromised children ensure appropriate immunizations are provided to these patients and their household and community contacts. We will review available data supporting the current guidelines regarding vaccine dosing, scheduling, and formulations to prevent influenza, COVID-19, and RSV infections in immunocompromised children. Furthermore, we highlight key knowledge gaps and areas of current investigation aimed at improving respiratory viral vaccine immunogenicity and optimize protection.
View review five-element analysis
Scope and question
The review focuses on immunocompromised pediatric patients, including hematopoietic cell and solid organ transplant recipients, those undergoing chemotherapy for malignancy, and those receiving biologic response modifiers for autoimmune or inflammatory conditions, who are at risk for severe disease from vaccine-preventable respiratory viral infections such as influenza, SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The central question is to review available data supporting current guidelines regarding vaccine dosing, scheduling, and formulations to prevent these infections in immunocompromised children.
Evidence base and method
The review is a narrative synthesis of available data, as no specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or study counts are reported. The authors aim to review existing guidelines and highlight knowledge gaps, but no systematic search or meta-analysis is described.
Consensus and conclusions
Immunocompromised children face higher rates of hospitalization, intensive care admissions, and mortality due to factors such as an immature immune system, absence of immunologic memory, and increased environmental exposures. Current immunization recommendations are largely extrapolated from studies in healthy children and/or immunocompromised adults due to a lack of primary data on immunological responses and vaccine efficacy in this population.
Controversies and gaps
There is a paucity of primary data on immunological responses and vaccine efficacy specifically in immunocompromised children. Additionally, trends in vaccine hesitancy, ongoing community transmission, and suboptimal vaccination rates among immunocompromised children and their household contacts compound the risk. Key knowledge gaps exist regarding improving respiratory viral vaccine immunogenicity and optimizing protection.
Research and practice implications
As the number of children with immunocompromising conditions expands, it is imperative that primary care practitioners and subspecialists ensure appropriate immunizations are provided to these patients and their household and community contacts. Future research should focus on improving vaccine immunogenicity and protection in this vulnerable population.

Remdesivir from failed Ebola drug to first FDA-approved COVID-19 antiviral: The medico-legal integration

Remdesivir from failed Ebola drug to first FDA-approved COVID-19 antiviral: The medico-legal integration
作者： Tung-Hu Tsai
摘要中文翻译
查看综述五要素
范围与问题
Remdesivir became the first antiviral for COVID-19 to receive emergency use authorization (EUA) and, subsequently, full FDA approval.
证据基础与方法
本文使用结合理论和文件分析的定性监管科学方法,对其开发生命周期进行了法定分析,追踪了九项美国联邦法规从基础冠状病毒科学到完全批准的贡献。
共识与结论
每个法规都映射到一个分阶段的生命周期框架。这些相互依存的法规共同展示了综合法律架构如何将开发压缩到数月之内。
争议与缺口
The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, under 42 U.S.C. § 282, designed and ran the pivotal the adaptive COVID-19 treatment trial (ACTT-1), generating EUA-supporting evidence in 14 weeks; Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority’s (BARDA) Other Transaction Authority enabled at-risk manufacturing before the EUA; the Project BioShield Act addressed the market failure of an intravenous, hospital-only antiviral; and the Defense Production Act supported domestic supply.
科研与实践启示
维持这一机构基础设施是大流行病防范中最重要的投资。

Remdesivir from failed Ebola drug to first FDA-approved COVID-19 antiviral: The medico-legal integration

Authors: Tung-Hu Tsai
Original abstract (English)
Summary Remdesivir became the first antiviral for COVID-19 to receive emergency use authorization (EUA) and, subsequently, full FDA approval. This article provides a statutory analysis of its development life cycle, tracing the contributions of nine US federal statutes from foundational coronavirus science through full approval, using a qualitative regulatory-science method that combines doctrinal and document analysis. Each statute is mapped onto a staged life cycle framework. The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, under 42 U.S.C. § 282, designed and ran the pivotal the adaptive COVID-19 treatment trial (ACTT-1), generating EUA-supporting evidence in 14 weeks; Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority’s (BARDA) Other Transaction Authority enabled at-risk manufacturing before the EUA; the Project BioShield Act addressed the market failure of an intravenous, hospital-only antiviral; and the Defense Production Act supported domestic supply. Together, these interdependent statutes show how an integrated legal architecture compressed development into months. Sustaining this institutional infrastructure is the most consequential investment in pandemic preparedness.

Research and practice implications
Sustaining this institutional infrastructure is the most consequential investment in pandemic preparedness.

作者： Jagdish Khubchandani, Nia Prabhu, Karishma Craig, Michael Wiblishauser, Toheeb Mustapha, Refat R. Srejon, Kavita Batra
摘要中文翻译
查看综述五要素
范围与问题
This scoping review investigated the nature and extent of COVID-19 vaccine refusal and non-uptake among people living with HIV (PLWH) in the USA.
证据基础与方法
A comprehensive literature search was performed utilizing multiple scholarly databases for studies published between December 2020 and May 2026 that reported on COVID-19 vaccine refusal or non-uptake rates among PLWH in the USA. A total of 27 studies were included, encompassing 185,430 PLWH from various settings across the U.S.
共识与结论
The refusal and non-uptake rates for COVID-19 vaccines among PLWH in the USA are considerable and influenced by multiple factors. The COVID-19 vaccination refusal and non-uptake rates varied from 3.8% to 57.9% [average across all studies=21.0% (95% CI=16.2-26.2%)].
争议与缺口
确定的主要障碍包括医疗不信任、对 疫苗 安全性和副作用的担忧、错误信息、贫困和住房不稳定等结构性问题以及社会人口因素(例如性/族裔少数地位、收入或教育程度较低)。
